rules.rule_name: Session Context Initialization on Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the program is being accessed for the first time or as a returning session, and initializes or restores the communication area accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Entry and Context Initialization
Check COMMAREA length & originating program
Initialize working storage & communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user accesses the Account View program
acceptance_criteria.When: The communication area length is zero (no prior session), OR the originating program is the Main Menu and the program re-entry flag is not set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initializes a fresh CARDDEMO communication area and the program-specific communication area, discarding any prior session data

rules.rule_name: Session Context Restoration on Re-entry
rules.rule_description: Restores the previously saved session state from the communication area when the user is returning to the program after a prior interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Entry and Context Initialization
Check COMMAREA length & originating program
Initialize working storage & communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user returns to the Account View program with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The communication area length is greater than zero AND the entry is not a fresh navigation from the Main Menu
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system restores the CARDDEMO communication area from the first portion of the saved communication area, and restores the program-specific communication area from the remaining portion

rules.rule_name: Accepted Function Key Identification
rules.rule_description: Captures the function key pressed by the user and maps it to a named key indicator. Supports ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, and PF1 through PF24 (where PF13-PF24 map to PF01-PF12 equivalents).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: PF Key Validation
Capture function key pressed
Accept Enter or PF3 only

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key (ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, PF1–PF24)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the pressed key as a named indicator: ENTER maps to CCARD-AID-ENTER; CLEAR maps to CCARD-AID-CLEAR; PA1 maps to CCARD-AID-PA1; PA2 maps to CCARD-AID-PA2; PF1/PF13 map to PFK01; PF2/PF14 map to PFK02; PF3/PF15 map to PFK03; PF4/PF16 map to PFK04; PF5/PF17 map to PFK05; PF6/PF18 map to PFK06; PF7/PF19 map to PFK07; PF8/PF20 map to PFK08; PF9/PF21 map to PFK09; PF10/PF22 map to PFK10; PF11/PF23 map to PFK11; PF12/PF24 map to PFK12

rules.rule_name: Unsupported Key Override to ENTER
rules.rule_description: Enforces that only ENTER and PF3 are valid user actions. Any other key press is silently overridden to behave as an ENTER key press.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: PF Key Validation
Capture function key pressed
Accept Enter or PF3 only

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and presses a key
acceptance_criteria.When: The pressed key is neither ENTER nor PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overrides the key action and treats it as if the user pressed ENTER, proceeding with normal input processing

rules.rule_name: Back Navigation via PF3 to Calling Program or Main Menu
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3, the system navigates back to the originating program and transaction. If no originating program or transaction is recorded, the system defaults to the Main Menu.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Navigation to Previous Screen or Main Menu
Determine calling program & transaction
Return to originating program or main menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3 (or PF15)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system determines the destination: if the originating transaction ID is blank or low-values, the destination transaction is set to the Main Menu transaction ID; otherwise the destination is set to the originating transaction ID. Similarly, if the originating program is blank or low-values, the destination program is set to the Main Menu program; otherwise it is set to the originating program. The current program and transaction are recorded as the 'from' context, the user type is set to USER, the program state is set to ENTER, and control is transferred to the destination program passing the updated communication area

rules.rule_name: Initial Blank Account View Screen Display on First Entry
rules.rule_description: On the first entry to the Account View program, the system displays a blank screen and prompts the user to enter an account number without any pre-populated data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Display Initial Account View Screen
Show blank Account View screen
Prompt user to enter account number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user navigates to the Account View program for the first time (program state is ENTER)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects it is in the initial entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system builds and sends the Account View screen with no account or customer data populated, and sets the prompt-for-input message to guide the user to enter an account number

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Population with Current Date and Time
rules.rule_description: Every time the Account View screen is displayed, the system populates the screen header with standard identification and current date/time information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Screen Header Initialization
Populate title, transaction ID, program name
Current date MM/DD/YY & time HH:MM:SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization routine executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the screen output area (CACTVWAO) to low-values, then populates: Title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), Transaction name (LIT-THISTRANID), Program name (LIT-THISPGM), Current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (using month digits 1-2, day digits 3-4, and year digits 3-4 of the 4-digit year), and Current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (using hours, minutes, and seconds)

rules.rule_name: Capture User-Entered Account Number from Screen
rules.rule_description: Retrieves the data entered by the user on the Account View screen, specifically the account number field, for subsequent validation and processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Receive User Input from Screen
Capture account number entered by user

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered data on the Account View screen and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the user's re-entry submission
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system receives the screen input into the CACTVWAI input map area, capturing the account ID field (ACCTSIDI) and any other screen fields entered by the user

rules.rule_name: Account Number Blank Input Validation
rules.rule_description: Validates that the user has entered a value in the account number field. If the field contains an asterisk or spaces, it is treated as blank.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Account Number Input Validation
Check if account number is blank
Check if non-numeric or zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user submits the Account View screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The account ID field (ACCTSIDI) contains an asterisk ('*') or spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the internal account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) to low-values (blank), sets the INPUT-ERROR flag, sets the FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK flag, sets the CDEMO-ACCT-ID to zero, and if no prior error message is active, sets the prompt message to request the user to enter an account number

rules.rule_name: Account Number Non-Numeric or Zero Validation
rules.rule_description: Validates that the account number entered by the user is a numeric, non-zero value. The account number must be an 11-digit non-zero numeric value.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Account Number Input Validation
Check if account number is blank
Check if non-numeric or zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user submits the Account View screen with a non-blank account number
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) is not numeric OR equals zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the INPUT-ERROR flag, sets the FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK flag, sets CDEMO-ACCT-ID to zero, and if no prior error message is active, displays the error message: 'Account Filter must  be a non-zero 11 digit number'

rules.rule_name: Valid Account Number Acceptance
rules.rule_description: Accepts and stores the account number when it passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, and non-zero).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Account Number Input Validation
Check if account number is blank
Check if non-numeric or zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user submits the Account View screen with an account number
acceptance_criteria.When: The entered account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) is numeric AND not equal to zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the entered account ID to CDEMO-ACCT-ID and sets the FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID flag to indicate the account filter is valid

rules.rule_name: No Search Criteria Received Detection
rules.rule_description: After individual field validation, performs a cross-field check to confirm that at least one search criterion (account number) has been provided before attempting a data lookup.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Cross-Field Validation
Check if no search criteria provided
Set No Input Received message

acceptance_criteria.Given: Individual account number field validation has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The account filter flag is set to BLANK (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is true)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED indicator to signal that no valid search input was provided and a data lookup should not be attempted

rules.rule_name: Account Card Cross-Reference Lookup by Account ID
rules.rule_description: Looks up the submitted account ID in the Card Cross-Reference alternate index file (CXACAIX) to retrieve the associated customer ID and card number required for subsequent data retrieval.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Account Card Cross-Reference Lookup
Look up account ID in Card Cross-Reference file

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid account ID has been entered and passed all input validations
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a read on the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) using the account ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account is found: the associated customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-ID and the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) is stored in CDEMO-CARD-NUM. If the account is not found: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the error message is set to 'Account: [account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'

rules.rule_name: Account Master Data Retrieval by Account ID
rules.rule_description: Retrieves the full account record from the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) using the account ID, after the account has been confirmed to exist in the Cross-Reference file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Account Master Data Retrieval
Read Account Master file using account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account ID has been successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a read on the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) using the account ID as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account record is found: the FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag is set and the full account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) is available for display. If the account record is not found: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the error message is set to 'Account: [account ID] not found in Acct Master file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'

rules.rule_name: Customer Master Data Retrieval by Customer ID
rules.rule_description: Retrieves the full customer record from the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the customer ID obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup, after the account has been confirmed in the Account Master.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Customer Master Data Retrieval
Read Customer Master file using customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a read on the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the customer ID (WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID, sourced from CDEMO-CUST-ID) as the key
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the customer record is found: the FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set and the full customer record (CUSTOMER-RECORD) is available for display. If the customer record is not found: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the error message is set to 'CustId: [customer ID] not found in customer master. Resp: [response code] REAS: [reason code]'

rules.rule_name: Account Data Population on Screen
rules.rule_description: Populates the Account View screen with account-level financial and status information when the account has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master or Customer Master file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Account Data Population on Screen
Populate active status, balance, credit limit
cash limit, cycle credits/debits, dates, group ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display after a data lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag OR the FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set to true
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the following account fields on the screen: Account Active Status (ACSTTUSO), Current Balance (ACURBALO), Credit Limit (ACRDLIMO), Cash Credit Limit (ACSHLIMO), Current Cycle Credit Amount (ACRCYCRO), Current Cycle Debit Amount (ACRCYDBO), Account Open Date (ADTOPENO), Account Expiration Date (AEXPDTO), Account Reissue Date (AREISDTO), and Account Group ID (AADDGRPO)

rules.rule_name: Customer Data Population on Screen
rules.rule_description: Populates the Account View screen with customer personal and contact information when the customer has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file. SSN is formatted with dashes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Customer Data Population on Screen
Populate customer ID, SSN, FICO score, DOB
name, address, phone numbers, govt ID, EFT

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display after a data lookup
acceptance_criteria.When: The FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set to true
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system populates the following customer fields on the screen: Customer ID (ACSTNUMO), Social Security Number formatted as XXX-XX-XXXX using characters 1-3, a dash, characters 4-5, a dash, and characters 6-9 of CUST-SSN (ACSTSSNO), FICO Credit Score (ACSTFCOO), Date of Birth in YYYY-MM-DD format (ACSTDOBO), First Name (ACSFNAMO), Middle Name (ACSMNAMO), Last Name (ACSLNAMO), Address Line 1 (ACSADL1O), Address Line 2 (ACSADL2O), City/Address Line 3 (ACSCITYO), State Code (ACSSTTEO), ZIP Code (ACSZIPCO), Country Code (ACSCTRYO), Phone Number 1 (ACSPHN1O), Phone Number 2 (ACSPHN2O), Government Issued ID (ACSGOVTO), EFT Account ID (ACSEFTCO), and Primary Card Holder Indicator (ACSPFLGO)

rules.rule_name: Account ID Field Display Based on Filter State
rules.rule_description: Controls how the account ID field is displayed on screen based on whether a valid account filter value exists.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Account Data Population on Screen
Populate active status, balance, credit limit
cash limit, cycle credits/debits, dates, group ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the session is not a fresh entry (EIBCALEN is not zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The account filter flag is BLANK (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the account ID display field (ACCTSIDO) to low-values. When the account filter flag is not blank, the system populates the account ID display field (ACCTSIDO) with the current account ID value (CC-ACCT-ID)

rules.rule_name: Screen Field Attribute and Color Setup for Account ID
rules.rule_description: Sets the visual attributes of the Account ID field on screen, including cursor positioning and color coding to indicate validation errors.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Screen Field Attribute and Color Setup
Set cursor on account ID field
Apply red highlight for errors
Set info message display color

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine executes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system always: sets the account ID field to protected/secure attribute (DFHBMFSE on ACCTSIDA), positions the cursor on the account ID field (length set to -1 on ACCTSIDL), and sets the account ID field color to default (DFHDFCOL on ACCTSIDC). Additionally: if FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is true, the account ID field color is changed to RED (DFHRED). If FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is true AND the program is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), the account ID display field is set to '*' and the field color is changed to RED

rules.rule_name: Informational Message Color Display Control
rules.rule_description: Controls the display color of the informational message area on the screen based on whether an active informational message exists.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Screen Field Attribute and Color Setup
Set cursor on account ID field
Apply red highlight for errors
Set info message display color

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine evaluates the informational message state
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is true (no active informational message), the info message field color is set to dark/non-display (DFHBMDAR on INFOMSGC). If an informational message is active, the info message field color is set to neutral (DFHNEUTR on INFOMSGC)

rules.rule_name: Error Message Display and Screen Refresh on Validation Failure
rules.rule_description: When input validation fails, the system redisplays the Account View screen with the error message visible and the cursor positioned on the account ID field to guide the user to correct the input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Error Message Display and Screen Refresh
Display screen with error messages in red
Cursor positioned on account ID field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Account View screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The INPUT-ERROR flag is set due to a validation failure (blank account, non-numeric account, zero account, or account not found in any data source)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the error message (WS-RETURN-MSG) to the screen error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), rebuilds the screen with current data and error highlighting, positions the cursor on the account ID field, highlights the account ID field in RED, and redisplays the screen to the user

rules.rule_name: Account View Processing Orchestration on Valid Input
rules.rule_description: Orchestrates the complete account data retrieval sequence when the user provides a valid account number, coordinating the three-step lookup process across Cross-Reference, Account Master, and Customer Master files.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Account View Processing Orchestration
Coordinate complete account retrieval sequence

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted a valid account number that passes all input validations
acceptance_criteria.When: The program is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) and no INPUT-ERROR flag is set after validation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system executes the account retrieval sequence in order: (1) performs the Card Cross-Reference lookup (9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT); if the account filter is not OK after this step, processing stops. (2) If cross-reference succeeds, performs the Account Master retrieval (9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT); if account not found, processing stops. (3) If account master succeeds, sets CDEMO-CUST-ID to WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID and performs the Customer Master retrieval (9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST). After the sequence completes, the screen is rebuilt and redisplayed with all retrieved data

rules.rule_name: Informational Message and Prompt Management
rules.rule_description: Manages the display of informational and prompt messages on the Account View screen, ensuring the user receives appropriate guidance based on the current state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17: Informational Message Management
Display prompt or account display confirmation message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen variable setup routine evaluates the message state
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is true, the system sets the prompt-for-input message (WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT) to guide the user. The current return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) is always moved to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO of CACTVWAO), and the current informational message (WS-INFO-MSG) is always moved to the screen info message field (INFOMSGO of CACTVWAO)

rules.rule_name: Return Control with Packaged Communication Area
rules.rule_description: Packages the complete session state into the communication area and returns control to the CICS transaction manager, preserving all context for the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Return Control with Communication Area
Package COMMAREA with program context
Return to CICS transaction manager

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen has been sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the COMMON-RETURN point
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system copies the current error/return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) to the screen error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), packages the CARDDEMO communication area into the first portion of WS-COMMAREA, packages the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) into the remaining portion of WS-COMMAREA starting after the CARDDEMO area, and issues a CICS RETURN with the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) and the fully packaged WS-COMMAREA, suspending execution until the user's next interaction

rules.rule_name: Detect New Session - No Prior Session Data
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the program is being accessed for the very first time in a new session by checking if there is no communication area data passed from a previous interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Communication Area Empty?
No prior session data?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user initiates the Account View program
acceptance_criteria.When: There is no communication area data available from any prior session (the session data length is zero, indicating no previous interaction exists)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a brand-new session with no prior context, and routes processing to perform a complete fresh initialization of all application and program-specific data areas

rules.rule_name: Detect New Request from Main Menu
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the user has navigated to the Account View program freshly from the Main Menu without any prior re-entry flag, which also requires a clean slate initialization even when prior session data technically exists.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Originating Program
the Main Menu AND
Not a Re-entry?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user accesses the Account View program and prior session data exists (communication area length is non-zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The originating program is identified as the Main Menu program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals the Main Menu program identifier) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (meaning this is not a return from a previous submission on this screen)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a new request originating from the Main Menu and routes processing to perform a complete fresh initialization, discarding any previously held session data

rules.rule_name: Fresh Start - Reset All Session Data
rules.rule_description: When the program is entered fresh (either as a brand-new session or as a new request from the Main Menu), all application-level and program-specific communication areas are fully reset to ensure no stale data from any prior session influences the current interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Fresh Start:
Reset Application Communication Area
Reset Program Communication Area
Start with clean slate

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined this is either a brand-new session (no prior session data) OR a new request arriving from the Main Menu without a re-entry flag
acceptance_criteria.When: The fresh start initialization is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the Application Communication Area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to its initial empty state AND resets the Program-Specific Communication Area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) to its initial empty state, ensuring the user starts with a completely clean slate with no residual data from any previous session

rules.rule_name: Re-entry - Restore Application Communication Area
rules.rule_description: When a returning user with an active session re-enters the program (e.g., after submitting an account number), the application-level communication area is restored from the previously saved session data so that shared application context (such as user type, transaction routing, and navigation history) is preserved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Re-entry:
Restore Application Communication Area
from previous session
Restore Program-specific Context
from previous session

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Account View program with an active session (prior session data exists) AND the program is NOT being accessed fresh from the Main Menu
acceptance_criteria.When: The re-entry restoration process is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system restores the Application Communication Area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) by reading the first portion of the saved session data, exactly matching the defined length of the Application Communication Area, so that all shared application-level context from the prior interaction is fully recovered

rules.rule_name: Re-entry - Restore Program-Specific Context
rules.rule_description: When a returning user with an active session re-enters the program, the program-specific context (such as previously entered account filter values and screen state) is restored from the saved session data immediately following the application communication area, ensuring continuity of the user's prior interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Re-entry:
Restore Application Communication Area
from previous session
Restore Program-specific Context
from previous session

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Account View program with an active session (prior session data exists) AND the program is NOT being accessed fresh from the Main Menu
acceptance_criteria.When: The re-entry restoration process is triggered after the Application Communication Area has been restored
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system restores the Program-Specific Communication Area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) by reading the second portion of the saved session data, starting immediately after the Application Communication Area's length boundary and spanning exactly the defined length of the Program-Specific Communication Area, so that all program-level context (such as previously entered account ID and screen state flags) from the prior interaction is fully recovered

rules.rule_name: Capture and Identify User Function Key Press
rules.rule_description: When a user interacts with the Account View screen, the system must identify and record which function key was pressed. Each key press is mapped to a specific internal key identifier so the system can determine the user's intended action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture the Function Key Pressed by User

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and presses a function key or action key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the key press input from the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies and records the key pressed as one of the following internal key identifiers: ENTER key is recorded as CCARD-AID-ENTER; PF3 (or PF15) key is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK03; PF1 (or PF13) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK01; PF2 (or PF14) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK02; PF4 (or PF16) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK04; PF5 (or PF17) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK05; PF6 (or PF18) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK06; PF7 (or PF19) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK07; PF8 (or PF20) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK08; PF9 (or PF21) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK09; PF10 (or PF22) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK10; PF11 (or PF23) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK11; PF12 (or PF24) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK12; CLEAR key is recorded as CCARD-AID-CLEAR; PA1 key is recorded as CCARD-AID-PA1; PA2 key is recorded as CCARD-AID-PA2. Note: PF13-PF24 are treated as aliases for PF1-PF12 respectively.

rules.rule_name: Default All Key Presses to Invalid Status
rules.rule_description: After capturing the key pressed by the user, the system initially marks the key status as INVALID by default before performing any validation. This ensures that only explicitly approved keys are treated as valid actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Key Status as INVALID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has captured and identified the function key pressed by the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The key identification step is complete, regardless of which key was pressed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the key validation status to INVALID as the default state, so that no key is considered valid unless it explicitly passes the subsequent validation check

rules.rule_name: Validate Accepted Function Keys - Enter and PF3 Only
rules.rule_description: The Account View screen only accepts two specific function keys as valid user inputs: the ENTER key and the PF3 key. All other key presses are not recognized as valid actions for this screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Key Enter or PF3?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has captured the user's key press and defaulted the key status to INVALID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the pressed key is either the ENTER key (CCARD-AID-ENTER) or the PF3 key (CCARD-AID-PFK03)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the pressed key is ENTER or PF3, the system marks the key status as VALID and proceeds with the identified key action; if the pressed key is any other key (e.g., PF1, PF2, PF4 through PF24, CLEAR, PA1, PA2), the key status remains INVALID

rules.rule_name: Mark Valid Key Status for Accepted Keys
rules.rule_description: When the user presses either the ENTER key or the PF3 key, the system explicitly marks the key status as VALID, allowing normal processing to continue with the specific action associated with that key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Key Status as VALID
Proceed with identified key

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the pressed key and determined it is either the ENTER key or the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.When: The key is confirmed to be ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER) or PF3 (CCARD-AID-PFK03)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the key validation status to VALID (PFK-VALID = TRUE) and continues processing using the specific action associated with the identified key (ENTER for data submission or PF3 for back/exit navigation)

rules.rule_name: Override Unsupported Key Press to ENTER Key
rules.rule_description: When a user presses any key that is not ENTER or PF3, the system overrides the key press and treats it as if the user had pressed the ENTER key. This ensures the screen continues normal processing without interruption, regardless of unsupported key presses.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Override Key:
Treat as ENTER Key
Continue Normal Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the pressed key and determined that the key status is INVALID (i.e., the key pressed was not ENTER or PF3)
acceptance_criteria.When: The key validation status is INVALID (PFK-INVALID = TRUE), meaning the user pressed any key other than ENTER or PF3 such as PF1, PF2, PF4-PF24, CLEAR, PA1, or PA2
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overrides the captured key identifier and sets it to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER = TRUE), so that subsequent processing continues as if the user had pressed the ENTER key, enabling normal screen processing to proceed

rules.rule_name: Determine Destination Transaction on PF3 Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 to navigate back, the system determines which transaction to return to. If no originating transaction was recorded in the session, the system defaults to the Main Menu transaction; otherwise, it routes back to the transaction that originally called this screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was a Calling Transaction Identified?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Account View screen and the session communication area contains the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) is blank or empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) is set to the Main Menu Transaction (LIT-MENUTRANID); otherwise, the destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) is set to the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)

rules.rule_name: Determine Destination Program on PF3 Press
rules.rule_description: After determining the destination transaction, the system also determines which program to transfer control to. If no originating program was recorded in the session, the system defaults to the Main Menu program; otherwise, it routes back to the program that originally invoked this screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was a Calling Program Identified?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Account View screen and the session communication area contains the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) is blank or empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is set to the Main Menu Program (LIT-MENUPGM); otherwise, the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is set to the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)

rules.rule_name: Update Communication Area with Current Program Context Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system updates the shared communication area to record the Account View program and transaction as the originating source, sets the user type to standard User, marks the program state as a Fresh Entry (not a re-entry), and records the current map and mapset as the last visited screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Update Communication Area
Record current program & transaction
as the originating source
Mark program state as Fresh Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) and destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) have been determined after the user pressed PF3
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the destination program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The communication area is updated as follows: the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) is set to the current Account View transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID); the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) is set to the current Account View program name (LIT-THISPGM); the user type (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER) is set to standard User; the program entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is marked as Fresh Entry; the last visited mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET) is set to the current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET); and the last visited map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) is set to the current map (LIT-THISMAP)

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Updated Communication Area
rules.rule_description: After updating the communication area with the current program context, the system transfers control to the resolved destination program, passing the full updated communication area so the receiving program has complete session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Transfer Control to
Destination Program
with Updated Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been determined and the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has been updated with the current program context
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer on PF3 press
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, and the full updated communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the receiving program so it has complete session and navigation context

rules.rule_name: Detect Fresh Program Entry and Initialize Session
rules.rule_description: Determines whether the Account View program is being accessed for the first time (fresh entry) — either because no prior session exists or because the user navigated from the Main Menu without re-entering — and initializes all session data accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Program Entered for First Time
Fresh Entry Detected

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user initiates the Account View program
acceptance_criteria.When: There is no prior session communication area (EIBCALEN equals zero), OR the program was called from the Main Menu program and the re-entry flag is not set
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system treats this as a fresh entry: all shared application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) are fully initialized to their default empty state, discarding any prior session data

rules.rule_name: Clear All Screen Output Fields Before Display
rules.rule_description: Before populating the Account View screen with any data, all screen output fields must be cleared to ensure no residual data from a previous interaction is inadvertently displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Initialize Screen Output Area
Clear all screen fields to low values

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Account View screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (1100-SCREEN-INIT) is invoked as part of the send-map process
acceptance_criteria.Then: All fields in the Account View screen output area (CACTVWAO) are set to low values, effectively blanking the entire screen before any new data is populated

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Application Identity and Current Date/Time
rules.rule_description: Every time the Account View screen is displayed, the screen header must be populated with the application titles, the current transaction ID, the current program name, and the real-time current date and time to provide the user with context and orientation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Screen Header
Application title, Transaction ID
Program name, Current date & time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is initializing the Account View screen for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (1100-SCREEN-INIT) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: (1) Application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) in the TITLE01O field, (2) Application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) in the TITLE02O field, (3) The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) in the TRNNAMEO field, (4) The current program name (LIT-THISPGM) in the PGMNAMEO field, (5) The current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY in the CURDATEO field, and (6) The current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS in the CURTIMEO field

rules.rule_name: Set Prompt-for-Input Mode on Fresh Entry
rules.rule_description: When the Account View screen is being displayed for the first time with no prior session data, the system must set the display mode to 'prompt for input' so that no account or customer data fields are populated and the user is guided to enter an account number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is this a Fresh Entry?
No prior COMMAREA?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is setting up the screen variables for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The communication area length (EIBCALEN) equals zero, indicating no prior session exists
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the display mode flag to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT (true), which causes all account data fields and customer data fields on the screen to remain blank — no account status, balances, credit limits, dates, customer name, address, or any other account/customer information is shown

rules.rule_name: Display Input Prompt Message When No Account Data is Present
rules.rule_description: When the screen is in prompt-for-input mode (no account data to display), the informational message area must show a prompt guiding the user to enter an account ID. Additionally, if no informational message is available, the prompt-for-input mode is re-enforced.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Informational Message
Display prompt:
'Enter or update id of account to display'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is finalizing screen variable setup for the Account View screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is true (no informational message has been set by prior processing)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system re-sets the display mode to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT (true); the current return/error message (WS-RETURN-MSG) is moved to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO), and the current informational message (WS-INFO-MSG — which contains the prompt 'Enter or update id of account to display') is moved to the screen informational message field (INFOMSGO) for display to the user

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor on Account ID Field and Apply Default Field Colors
rules.rule_description: On the initial blank Account View screen, the cursor must be positioned on the Account ID input field to guide the user, the field must be set to its default color (no error highlighting), and the informational message area color must reflect whether a message is present.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Position Cursor on Account ID Field
Apply default color to Account ID field
No red highlighting needed - no errors yet

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is setting screen display attributes for the Account View screen prior to sending it to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is executed for a fresh entry with no validation errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system: (1) Sets the Account ID field (ACCTSIDA) to protected/secure attribute (DFHBMFSE), (2) Sets the cursor length indicator (ACCTSIDL) to -1 to position the cursor on the Account ID field regardless of filter status, (3) Sets the Account ID field color (ACCTSIDC) to the default color (DFHDFCOL) — no red highlighting since there are no errors, and (4) Sets the informational message field color (INFOMSGC) to dark/suppressed (DFHBMDAR) if no informational message is present, or to neutral color (DFHNEUTR) if an informational message exists

rules.rule_name: Send Blank Account View Screen and Mark Session for Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: After all screen fields and attributes have been prepared, the Account View screen must be sent to the user's terminal with the screen cleared and the keyboard unlocked. The session state must be updated to 're-entry' mode so that the next user interaction is processed as a data submission.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Send Blank Account View Screen to User
Screen cleared and displayed
Keyboard unlocked for user input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen has been fully initialized with header, blank data fields, prompt message, cursor position, and field colors
acceptance_criteria.When: The send-screen routine (1400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system: (1) Records the current map name (LIT-THISMAP) and mapset name (LIT-THISMAPSET) as the next map/mapset to be used, (2) Sets the program state flag to CDEMO-PGM-REENTER (true) so the next user interaction will be treated as a re-entry/data submission, (3) Sends the Account View screen (CACTVWAO) to the user's terminal with the screen fully erased (ERASE) and the keyboard unlocked (FREEKB), with the cursor positioned on the Account ID field (CURSOR)

rules.rule_name: Invoke Screen Display Sequence on First Program Entry
rules.rule_description: When the Account View program is entered for the first time (program-enter state), the system must invoke the complete screen preparation and display sequence — covering initialization, variable setup, attribute setup, and screen transmission — before returning control to await user input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User Sees Blank Account View Screen
Ready to Enter Account Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View program has been entered and the session has been identified as a first-time (fresh) entry with the program state set to CDEMO-PGM-ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The main program logic evaluates the program state as CDEMO-PGM-ENTER
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system invokes the full send-map sequence (1000-SEND-MAP through 1000-SEND-MAP-EXIT), which in turn executes: screen initialization (1100-SCREEN-INIT), screen variable setup (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS), screen attribute setup (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS), and screen transmission (1400-SEND-SCREEN); after which control is passed to COMMON-RETURN to save session state and await the next user interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is about to be prepared for display to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header initialization process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen output fields on the Account View screen (CACTVWAO) must be cleared and reset to blank/low values before any new data is populated, ensuring a clean slate for the new screen display

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time
rules.rule_description: The system must retrieve the current date and time from the operating system to display accurate, real-time information on the Account View screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Current System Date & Time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen header initialization is in progress and all screen fields have been cleared

rules.rule_name: Populate Application Title Lines on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Account View screen header must display two lines of application title text to identify the application to the user. Both title lines are sourced from the application's standard title definitions.

Populate Application Titles
Title Line 1 & Title Line 2
on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.When: The application title section of the screen header is being populated

rules.rule_name: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Account View screen header must display the current transaction identifier so the user can identify which transaction they are working within.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Transaction ID
on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen header initialization is in progress and application titles have been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction identification section of the screen header is being populated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen header must be populated with the current transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) assigned to this Account View program

rules.rule_name: Populate Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The Account View screen header must display the current program name so the user and support staff can identify which program is currently executing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Program Name
on Screen Header

rules.rule_name: Format Current System Date as MM/DD/YY

rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Format as MM/DD/YY

acceptance_criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) must be extracted into WS-CURDATE-MM, the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) must be extracted into WS-CURDATE-DD, and only the last 2 digits of the year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) must be extracted into WS-CURDATE-YY, resulting in a combined date value in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY formatted as MM/DD/YY

rules.rule_name: Display Formatted Date on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.When: The date is being placed onto the screen header for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted date value (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) in MM/DD/YY format must be moved to the Current Date display field (CURDATEO) on the Account View screen header (CACTVWAO)

rules.rule_name: Format Current System Time as HH:MM:SS
rules.rule_description: The current system time must be decomposed into its individual components (hours, minutes, seconds) and formatted into the standard HH:MM:SS display format for the screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Extract Hours, Minutes & Seconds
Format as HH:MM:SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date and time have been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA, which also contains the time components
acceptance_criteria.When: The system time is being formatted for display on the screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) must be extracted into WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) must be extracted into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) must be extracted into WS-CURTIME-SS, resulting in a combined time value in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS formatted as HH:MM:SS

rules.rule_name: Display Formatted Time on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The formatted system time in HH:MM:SS format must be displayed in the designated time field on the Account View screen header.

rules.rule_description: When a returning user (re-entering the screen after a prior interaction) submits the screen without providing any Account ID value, the Account ID field must display an asterisk (*) as a visual placeholder and be highlighted in RED, signaling that the required Account ID was not provided.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Account ID left blank AND user is returning to the screen? → Yes - Blank on Re-entry → Display asterisk in Account ID Field, Apply RED color to Account ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the user has previously interacted with this screen (re-entry state is active)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID field was left blank (empty, spaces, or asterisk submitted) by the user on this return visit (Account Filter Blank flag is set AND program re-entry flag is active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: An asterisk character (*) is placed in the Account ID field as a visual placeholder, AND the Account ID field is highlighted in RED color to indicate that a required Account ID value was not provided

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether to Capture User Input Based on Program Entry State
rules.rule_description: The system determines whether the user has previously interacted with the Account View screen. Only when the program is in a re-entry state (user has already seen the screen and submitted data) should the system attempt to capture and process user input. On first entry, no input capture occurs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a Re-entry to Program?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has navigated to the Account View screen and the program is being invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the current program state flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER for first entry vs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER for subsequent interaction)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the program state is FIRST ENTRY (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER), the system bypasses all input capture and proceeds directly to display a fresh Account View screen. If the program state is RE-ENTRY (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), the system proceeds to capture and process the user-submitted input from the screen.

rules.rule_name: Capture User Input from Account View Screen on Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: When the user has submitted the Account View screen, the system captures all data entered by the user from the Account View screen map (CACTVWAI) into the working input area for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture User Input from Account View Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is in a re-entry state, meaning the user has previously been presented with the Account View screen and has pressed ENTER to submit their input
acceptance_criteria.When: The system receives the screen map data from the Account View screen (map: CACTVWAI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: All user-entered data from the Account View screen is captured into the program's input working area (CACTVWAI), making it available for subsequent retrieval and validation steps

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Account Number Entered by User from Screen Input
rules.rule_description: After capturing the screen input, the system retrieves the account number value entered by the user. If the user entered an asterisk ('*') or left the field blank (spaces), the account number is treated as not provided. Otherwise, the entered value is stored as the account number to be validated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Account Number Entered by User

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's screen input has been captured from the Account View screen into the input working area (CACTVWAI)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the Account ID input field (ACCTSIDI) from the captured screen data
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the Account ID field contains an asterisk ('*') or spaces, the account number (CC-ACCT-ID) is set to empty (LOW-VALUES), indicating no account number was provided. If the Account ID field contains any other value, that value is stored as the account number (CC-ACCT-ID) to be passed forward for validation.

rules.rule_name: Pass Captured Account Input for Validation Processing
rules.rule_description: Once the account number has been retrieved from the screen input, the system passes the captured input through the validation process. The sequence ensures that input capture always precedes validation, and the current program context (program name, map, mapset) is recorded for screen redisplay purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pass Captured Input for Validation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's account number input has been retrieved from the Account View screen and stored in the working area (CC-ACCT-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The input processing sequence completes the capture phase (2100-RECEIVE-MAP) and moves to the edit/validation phase (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The captured input is passed to the validation process (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS). The current program name (LIT-THISPGM), mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET), and map name (LIT-THISMAP) are recorded in the screen control area (CCARD-NEXT-PROG, CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET, CCARD-NEXT-MAP) to support subsequent screen redisplay. Any return message is also carried forward (WS-RETURN-MSG to CCARD-ERROR-MSG).

rules.rule_name: Display Fresh Account View Screen on First Program Entry Without Input Capture
rules.rule_description: When a user accesses the Account View screen for the first time (first program entry), the system does not attempt to capture or process any user input. Instead, it immediately displays a blank Account View screen prompting the user to enter an account number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No Input Capture - Display Fresh Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has been invoked and the program state indicates this is the first time the user is entering the Account View screen (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER state)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the program entry state and determines it is a first-time entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system skips all input capture and validation steps entirely, proceeds directly to build and send the Account View screen (1000-SEND-MAP), and returns control to wait for the user's first interaction. No account data lookup is performed.

rules.rule_name: Normalize Account Number Input - Treat Asterisk or Spaces as Blank
rules.rule_description: Before validating the account number, any entry of an asterisk ('*') or spaces in the Account Number field is treated as if no account number was provided, normalizing the input to a blank/empty value for downstream validation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Blank or Not Provided?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and has submitted the Account Number input field
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Number field contains an asterisk ('*') or only spaces
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Number is treated as blank (cleared to empty/low values) and is considered not provided, so that subsequent blank validation rules are triggered

rules.rule_name: Account Number Blank or Not Provided - Mandatory Field Validation
rules.rule_description: The Account Number is a mandatory input field. If the user submits the screen without entering an Account Number (field is empty or blank), an error must be raised and the user must be prompted to provide an Account Number before any account lookup can proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Blank or Not Provided?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and submits the form
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Number field is blank, empty, or contains only spaces (including when normalized from asterisk or spaces)
acceptance_criteria.Then: An input error flag is set, the Account Number filter is marked as blank, the stored Account ID is cleared to zero, and the user is prompted with a message to provide an Account Number; no account lookup is performed

rules.rule_name: Account Number Non-Numeric or Zero - Format Validation
rules.rule_description: The Account Number must be a numeric, non-zero value. If the user enters a value that contains non-numeric characters or is equal to zero, an error must be raised with a specific message indicating the required format.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Non-Numeric OR Equal to Zero?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen, has provided a non-blank Account Number, and submits the form
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Number contains non-numeric characters OR the Account Number equals zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: An input error flag is set, the Account Number filter is marked as invalid, the stored Account ID is cleared to zero, and the error message 'Account Filter must be a non-zero 11 digit number' is displayed to the user; no account lookup is performed

rules.rule_name: Valid Account Number - Store for Further Processing
rules.rule_description: When the Account Number passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, and non-zero), it is accepted as a valid input, stored for account lookup processing, and the Account Number filter is marked as valid to allow the account retrieval process to proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Account Number for Further Processing - Mark Account Filter as Valid

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and submits the form with an Account Number
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Number is non-blank, is fully numeric, and is not equal to zero
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Number is stored as the Account ID for further processing and the Account Number filter status is marked as valid, allowing the account lookup to proceed

rules.rule_name: No Search Criteria Received - Blank Account Filter Post-Validation
rules.rule_description: After account number validation, if the Account Number filter is determined to be blank, the system must additionally flag that no search criteria were received. This ensures the overall input processing correctly reflects that the user did not supply any searchable account information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number Blank or Not Provided?

acceptance_criteria.Given: Account Number input validation has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Number filter is marked as blank (no account number was provided by the user)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system additionally sets a flag indicating that no search criteria were received, confirming that account lookup cannot be initiated

rules.rule_name: Detect Missing Account Search Criteria After Field Validation
rules.rule_description: After individual account field validation completes, the system performs a cross-field check to determine whether the account filter was left blank. If no account number was provided by the user, the system sets a 'No Search Criteria Received' condition to prevent any data lookup from proceeding.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Account Filter Flag Marked as Blank During Field Validation?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The individual account field validation has completed and the Account Filter Flag has been marked as Blank (meaning the user submitted the screen without entering an Account ID — the field was empty, contained only spaces, or contained '*')
acceptance_criteria.When: The cross-field validation check evaluates whether the Account Filter Blank flag is active
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Search Criteria Received' condition to TRUE, indicating that the user provided no input to search on, and no account data lookup is initiated

rules.rule_name: Prompt User to Enter Account Number When Field Is Blank
rules.rule_description: When the Account ID field is found to be blank during individual field validation, and no prior error message has already been set in the session, the system sets a prompt message instructing the user to enter an account number. This prompt guides the user on the required action to proceed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Prompt Message Set: 'Enter account number to display'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Account View screen with the Account ID field left empty (blank, spaces, or containing '*'), and no error or return message has been previously set during the current interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The account field validation detects that the Account ID is equal to LOW-VALUES or SPACES (i.e., the Account Filter Blank flag is set to TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the prompt message to 'Enter account number to display' (WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT), marks the input as an error (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE), sets the Account Filter Flag to Blank, and clears the Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero — no account data lookup is performed

rules.rule_name: Use Account ID as Search Key for Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: When processing an account view request, the system must use the validated Account ID entered by the user as the key to search the Card Cross-Reference file to retrieve associated customer and card information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use entered Account ID as search key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid Account ID that has passed all input validations (non-blank, numeric, non-zero, 11-digit)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the account data retrieval process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the validated Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) as the search key (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID) to perform a lookup against the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX alternate index)

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Customer ID from Card Cross-Reference on Successful Lookup
rules.rule_description: When an account ID is successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must retrieve and store the associated Customer ID for use in subsequent customer data retrieval.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve and Store Customer ID associated with Account

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is found successfully in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must retrieve the Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) from the cross-reference record and store it as the active Customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) for use in the subsequent Customer Master lookup

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Card Number from Card Cross-Reference on Successful Lookup
rules.rule_description: When an account ID is successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must also retrieve and store the associated Card Number linked to that account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve and Store Card Number associated with Account

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) and the account has been found
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is found successfully in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must retrieve the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) from the cross-reference record and store it as the active Card Number (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) for the current session

rules.rule_name: Mark Account Filter as Invalid When Account Not Found in Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: When the entered Account ID cannot be located in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must flag the account filter as invalid and mark the overall input as an error to prevent further data retrieval processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Account Filter as Invalid

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX)
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account ID is NOT found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the input state to error (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE) and mark the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), preventing any further account or customer data retrieval

rules.rule_name: Build Account Not Found Error Message for Cross-Reference Lookup Failure
rules.rule_description: When an account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must construct and display a specific error message identifying the account that was searched and indicating it was not found in the cross-reference file, but only if no prior error message has already been set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Build Error Message: Account not found in Cross-Reference File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) has failed because the account was not found, and no prior error message has been set for the current transaction (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the account not-found condition from the Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must build an error message in the format: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [Response Code] Reas: [Reason Code]' and store it in WS-RETURN-MSG to be displayed to the user on the screen

rules.rule_name: Stop Account Data Retrieval Processing When Cross-Reference Lookup Fails
rules.rule_description: When the Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the account filter has been marked as invalid, the system must immediately stop all further account and customer data retrieval and return to display the error to the user without proceeding to Account Master or Customer Master lookups.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Stop Processing Display Error to User

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has failed and the account filter has been marked as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue with Account Master and Customer Master lookups
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must immediately stop all further data retrieval processing (skip Account Master lookup and Customer Master lookup) and proceed directly to display the error message to the user

rules.rule_name: Flag Account as Invalid When Not Found in Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When an account lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file returns no matching record, the account filter must be marked as invalid and the overall input must be flagged as an error, regardless of whether a prior error message already exists.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Account Filter as Invalid
Mark Input as Error

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has submitted an Account ID for lookup and the Card Cross-Reference file does not contain a record matching the submitted Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Cross-Reference file lookup returns a 'Not Found' result for the given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account Filter status must be set to 'Invalid' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK) AND the overall Input status must be set to 'Error' (INPUT-ERROR), indicating that the submitted account cannot be processed further

rules.rule_name: Check for Existing Error Message Before Building New Account Not Found Message
rules.rule_description: Before constructing a new error message for an account not found in the Cross-Reference file, the system must check whether an error message has already been set. If a prior error message exists, it must be preserved and no new message is constructed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Error Message
Area Currently Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the account filter has been marked as invalid and input flagged as error
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the error message area is currently empty (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE, meaning no prior error message has been set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the error message area is empty, proceed to build a new formatted error message; If the error message area already contains a prior message, skip message construction and preserve the existing error message

rules.rule_name: Capture Response and Reason Codes for Account Not Found Error
rules.rule_description: When an account is not found in the Cross-Reference file and no prior error message exists, the system response code and reason code from the failed file lookup must be captured and stored so they can be included in the error message displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Capture System Response Code
from file lookup attempt
Capture System Reason Code
from file lookup attempt

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the error message area is currently empty (no prior error message exists)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to build the account not found error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system response code from the file lookup attempt must be captured into ERROR-RESP AND the system reason code from the file lookup attempt must be captured into ERROR-RESP2, making both codes available for inclusion in the error message

rules.rule_name: Build Formatted Error Message for Account Not Found in Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When an account is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file and no prior error message exists, a detailed formatted error message must be constructed by combining the literal label 'Account:', the actual Account ID that was searched, the phrase 'not found in Cross ref file', the response code prefixed with 'Resp:', and the reason code prefixed with 'Reas:' into a single message string.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Build Error Message by combining:
'Account:' + Searched Account ID
+ 'not found in Cross ref file'
+ 'Resp:' + Response Code
+ 'Reas:' + Reason Code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the error message area is currently empty AND the response code and reason code from the failed lookup have been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The system constructs the account not found error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: A single formatted error message must be built by concatenating all of the following components in order: the literal text 'Account:' + the searched Account ID (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) + the literal text ' not found in Cross ref file.  Resp:' + the captured Response Code (ERROR-RESP) + the literal text ' Reas:' + the captured Reason Code (ERROR-RESP2), and the resulting message must be stored in the error message field (WS-RETURN-MSG) for display on the Account View screen

rules.rule_name: Store Formatted Account Not Found Error Message for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The fully constructed account not found error message must be stored in the designated screen error message field so it can be presented to the user on the Account View screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store Formatted Error Message
for display on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A formatted error message has been built combining the account ID, 'not found in Cross ref file' text, response code, and reason code
acceptance_criteria.When: The STRING operation completes building the error message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete formatted error message must be stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, which is the field used to display error messages on the Account View screen (ERRMSGO of CACTVWAO)

rules.rule_name: Stop Further Account Data Lookups When Account Not Found in Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: When an account is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, all subsequent data lookups (Account Master and Customer Master) must be immediately halted. The account lookup chain is a sequential dependency — without a valid Cross-Reference record, neither account details nor customer details can be retrieved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Return to Account View
Processing - Stop Further Lookups

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the account filter has been marked as invalid AND the input has been flagged as an error AND the error message has been set (either newly built or pre-existing)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue with the next step in the account data retrieval chain (Account Master lookup)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must immediately stop all further account data lookups — specifically, the Account Master file lookup (9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT) and the Customer Master file lookup (9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST) must NOT be executed — and control must return to the Account View processing to display the error to the user

rules.rule_name: Account Master File Lookup by Account ID
rules.rule_description: When processing an account view request, the system must retrieve full account details from the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the submitted Account ID as the search key.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Account ID as search key to look up Account Master File ACCTDAT

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid, non-zero, 11-digit numeric Account ID has passed all input validations and has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the search key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account record from the Account Master File into the Account Record data area, making all account details available for further processing and screen display

rules.rule_name: Account Record Found in Account Master - Mark Account as Available
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup successfully locates the account record, the system must flag the account as found so that all retrieved account details are made available for display on the Account View screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Account as Found - Account details available for screen display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the submitted Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Master File lookup returns a successful match — the account record exists in the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the account as found (FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag is set to TRUE), making all retrieved account details — including Account Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Reissue Date, and Group ID — available for display on the Account View screen

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found in Account Master - Set Error Indicator on Account ID Field
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup fails to locate the submitted Account ID, the system must flag the input as invalid and mark the Account ID field as erroneous to prevent further data retrieval and to trigger error display on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag on Account ID Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the submitted Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The Account Master File lookup finds no matching account record for the submitted Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the overall Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE) and marks the Account ID field filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), stopping any further data retrieval (Customer Master lookup is not performed)

rules.rule_name: Account Not Found in Account Master - Build User-Facing Error Message
rules.rule_description: When the Account Master File lookup fails to locate the submitted Account ID and no prior error message has been set, the system must construct and display a descriptive error message identifying the specific Account ID that was not found in the Account Master File.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Build Error Message: Account not found in Account Master File

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the INPUT-ERROR flag to TRUE, (2) Set the FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK flag to TRUE, (3) If no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE), set the error message WS-RETURN-MSG to 'Account Filter must be a non-zero 11 digit number', (4) Clear the internal account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (5) Stop further account validation

rules.rule_name: No Search Criteria Received Status Assignment

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user submits the Account View screen and the account ID field is blank, resulting in FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK being set to TRUE during account validation

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED status flag to TRUE, indicating that the user provided no account search criteria at all

rules.rule_name: Error Message Propagation to Screen Display Area
rules.rule_description: After input validation errors are detected, the system must transfer the error message from the internal working storage message field to the screen's designated error message display area so it is visible to the user on the refreshed screen.

acceptance_criteria.Given: Input validation has completed and an error condition exists (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE), with an error message stored in WS-RETURN-MSG
