acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must move the contents of WS-RETURN-MSG to the screen error message output field CCARD-ERROR-MSG (ERRMSGO of CACTVWAO), making the error message visible to the user on the refreshed screen

rules.rule_name: Cursor Positioning on Account ID Field for Error Correction
rules.rule_description: Whenever the Account View screen is displayed after a validation error — regardless of whether the account ID was blank or contained an invalid value — the system must always position the cursor on the Account ID input field to guide the user directly to the field requiring correction.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing screen attributes for the Account View screen after a validation error, where either FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE, FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is TRUE, or any other condition applies

rules.rule_name: Blank Account ID Field Highlighted Red with Asterisk Placeholder on Re-entry

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Display an asterisk character '*' in the Account ID output field (ACCTSIDO of CACTVWAO) as a visual placeholder, and (2) Set the color of the Account ID field (ACCTSIDC of CACTVWAO) to RED (DFHRED) to visually alert the user that the field requires a valid account number

rules.rule_name: Invalid Account ID Field Highlighted Red
rules.rule_description: When a user enters an Account ID value that fails validation (non-numeric or zero), the system must highlight the Account ID field in red on the refreshed screen to visually indicate to the user that the entered value is invalid.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered an Account ID value that failed validation, resulting in FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK being set to TRUE
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up screen display attributes for the Account View screen refresh
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the color attribute of the Account ID field (ACCTSIDC of CACTVWAO) to RED (DFHRED), visually signaling to the user that the entered account number is invalid and requires correction

rules.rule_name: Information Message Area Color Based on Message Availability
rules.rule_description: The system must control the visual appearance of the information message area on the Account View screen based on whether an informational message is available to display, using dark color when no message exists and neutral color when a message is present.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether an informational message is available (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag status)

rules.rule_name: Account View Screen Refresh and Display with Error Highlights
rules.rule_description: After all error messages and screen attributes have been prepared, the system must send the Account View screen to the user with all error highlights applied, the cursor positioned on the Account ID field, and the keyboard unlocked so the user can make corrections.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the screen send operation (1400-SEND-SCREEN) using the configured map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and mapset (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Mark the session as a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER set to TRUE) so the next user submission is processed as a correction attempt, (2) Send the Account View screen (CACTVWAO) to the user's terminal with the CURSOR option to position the cursor on the Account ID field, (3) Erase the previous screen content (ERASE), and (4) Unlock the keyboard (FREEKB) so the user can immediately type corrections

rules.rule_name: Display Prompt Message When No Informational Message Exists
rules.rule_description: When the informational message area on the Account View screen is empty (no info message has been set), the system should automatically set and display a prompt message guiding the user to enter or update the account ID they wish to view.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Info Message Area Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display AND the informational message area is empty (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is set to TRUE, indicating no informational message has been populated)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen setup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the prompt message 'Enter or update id of account to display' as the active input prompt (WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT is set to TRUE), and this prompt is rendered in a dark or dimmed color on the screen to indicate it is a guidance message rather than a data value

rules.rule_name: Display Confirmation Message When Account Data Is Successfully Retrieved
rules.rule_description: When account data has been successfully retrieved and is being displayed on the Account View screen, the informational message area should show a confirmation message 'Displaying details of given Account' rendered in a neutral color to indicate active data display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was Account Data Successfully Retrieved and Displayed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display AND the informational message area contains a message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is FALSE, meaning WS-INFO-MSG has been populated with a value such as 'Displaying details of given Account')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen attribute setup
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the informational message from WS-INFO-MSG in the INFOMSGO field on the screen, and the informational message area color attribute (INFOMSGC) is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), indicating that a valid informational message is actively being shown to the user

rules.rule_name: Apply Dark Color to Informational Message Area When No Message Exists
rules.rule_description: When the informational message area is empty (no info message set), the system must render the informational message area in a dark or dimmed color on the Account View screen to visually distinguish it from active informational content.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Prompt in Dark/Dim Color on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured AND the informational message area is empty (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is TRUE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the display color attributes for the informational message area on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message area color attribute (INFOMSGC of CACTVWAO) is set to dark or dimmed (DFHBMDAR), visually indicating to the user that no active informational message is present and the area contains only a background prompt

rules.rule_name: Apply Neutral Color to Informational Message Area When Message Is Present
rules.rule_description: When the informational message area contains an active message (such as a confirmation that account details are being displayed), the system must render the informational message area in a neutral color on the Account View screen to indicate active informational content.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Confirmation in Neutral Color on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured AND the informational message area contains an active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is FALSE, meaning WS-INFO-MSG has been populated)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the display color attributes for the informational message area on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message area color attribute (INFOMSGC of CACTVWAO) is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), visually indicating to the user that an active informational message is present and should be read

rules.rule_name: Reset Informational Message State at Start of Account Data Retrieval
rules.rule_description: At the beginning of every account data retrieval attempt, the informational message state is reset to 'no info message', ensuring that any previously displayed informational message is cleared before new account data lookup results are evaluated and a fresh message state is established.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Info Message Area Empty?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has passed all input validations AND the system is about to begin the account data retrieval process (entering the 9000-READ-ACCT routine)
acceptance_criteria.When: The account data retrieval process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The informational message flag is reset to indicate no informational message exists (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is set to TRUE), clearing any prior informational message state so that the screen message area reflects the outcome of the current retrieval attempt

rules.rule_name: Populate Informational Message Field on Screen from Message Storage
rules.rule_description: During screen variable setup, the current informational message stored in the working storage message field is transferred to the screen's informational message output field, ensuring the user sees the most current informational message (such as 'Displaying details of given Account') on the Account View screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Confirmation Message: 'Displaying details of given Account'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen variables are being set up for display AND the informational message working storage field (WS-INFO-MSG) contains a message value (e.g., 'Displaying details of given Account')
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen output fields with current data values
acceptance_criteria.Then: The content of the informational message working storage field (WS-INFO-MSG) is moved to the informational message output field (INFOMSGO of CACTVWAO) on the Account View screen, making the message visible to the user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the informational message area (WS-INFO-MSG) contains no active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is true)

rules.rule_name: Retain Existing Informational Message When Already Set
rules.rule_description: When an informational message is already present (e.g., 'Displaying details of given Account' after a successful account lookup), the system retains and displays that existing message without overwriting it.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the informational message area (WS-INFO-MSG) already contains an active message such as 'Displaying details of given Account'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen setup and finds that WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is false
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retains the existing informational message as-is and moves it to the screen output field (INFOMSGO), so the user sees the current status message without any overwrite

rules.rule_name: Set Informational Message Display Color to Dark When No Active Message
rules.rule_description: When there is no active informational message to display, the informational message area on screen is rendered in a dark or dimmed color, visually indicating to the user that no status information is currently available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Display Color: Dark / Dimmed - No active message to highlight

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured and the informational message area contains no active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is true)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the display color attribute for the informational message field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system applies a dark/dimmed color attribute (DFHBMDAR) to the informational message display area (INFOMSGC), visually suppressing the field since no message is active

rules.rule_name: Set Informational Message Display Color to Neutral When Active Message Present
rules.rule_description: When an active informational message exists and is ready to be shown to the user, the informational message area is rendered in a neutral (standard) color, making the message clearly visible and readable on screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Display Color: Neutral - Active message is present

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured and the informational message area contains an active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is false)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the display color attribute for the informational message field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system applies a neutral color attribute (DFHNEUTR) to the informational message display area (INFOMSGC), ensuring the active message is clearly visible to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Informational Message Content on Account View Screen
rules.rule_description: After the informational message content and display color have been determined, the system renders the complete Account View screen including the informational message area, making the prompt or status message visible to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Informational Message on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The informational message content (WS-INFO-MSG mapped to INFOMSGO) and its display color attribute (INFOMSGC) have both been set, and the full screen output area (CACTVWAO) is ready
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the Account View screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is displayed with the informational message area showing either the prompt text 'Enter or update id of account to display' in dark/dimmed color (when no active message) or the status message 'Displaying details of given Account' in neutral color (when an active message is present), with the cursor positioned and the keyboard unlocked for user input

rules.rule_name: Propagate Return Message to Communication Area Error Field
rules.rule_description: Before returning control to the transaction manager, any pending return or error message held in the working storage return message field must be copied into the communication area error message field so it is available for display on the next screen interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Copy any pending error or return message into the communication area error message field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is preparing to return control to the CICS transaction manager and there is a pending return message or error message stored in the working storage return message field (WS-RETURN-MSG)
acceptance_criteria.When: The return control sequence is initiated at the COMMON-RETURN point
acceptance_criteria.Then: The content of the working storage return message field (WS-RETURN-MSG) must be copied into the communication area error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG) so that the message is preserved and available for display during the next user interaction

rules.rule_name: Package Main Application Communication Area into Outgoing Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which holds shared application context including program navigation details, user type, and last map and mapset used, must be packaged into the first portion of the outgoing communication area before returning control.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Package main application communication area into the outgoing communication area Includes program context, user type, last map & mapset used

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is preparing to return control and the main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains current session context including the calling program, destination program, user type, last mapset used, and last map used
acceptance_criteria.When: The return control sequence is initiated at the COMMON-RETURN point
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire content of the main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the first portion of the outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA), preserving all program navigation context, user type, and map/mapset information for the next program interaction

rules.rule_name: Append Program-Specific Communication Area into Second Portion of Outgoing Communication Area
rules.rule_description: The program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which holds state information specific to this Account View program, must be appended into the second portion of the outgoing communication area immediately after the main application communication area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Append program-specific communication area into the second portion of the outgoing communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has already been packaged into the first portion of the outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contains the current program-level state
acceptance_criteria.When: The return control sequence is initiated at the COMMON-RETURN point
acceptance_criteria.Then: The content of the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be placed into the outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA) starting at the position immediately after the end of the main application communication area (offset = length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1), for a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, ensuring both areas are preserved contiguously in the outgoing communication area

rules.rule_name: Return Control to Transaction Manager Keeping Screen Active for Further User Interaction
rules.rule_description: After packaging all session and program-specific context into the outgoing communication area, control must be returned to the CICS transaction manager specifying the current transaction ID and the fully assembled communication area, so the screen remains active and the session state is preserved for the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return control to CICS Transaction Manager with current Transaction ID so screen remains active for further user interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully assembled with both the main application communication area and the program-specific communication area, and the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) identifies this Account View transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The return control sequence completes at the COMMON-RETURN point
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control must be returned to the CICS transaction manager specifying: (1) the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) so the same transaction is re-invoked on the next user action, (2) the fully assembled outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA) containing all session context, and (3) the full length of the outgoing communication area — ensuring the screen remains active and all session state is available for the next user interaction

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user accesses the Account View program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The communication area length is zero (no prior session), OR the originating program is the Main Menu and the program re-entry flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system initializes a fresh CARDDEMO communication area and the program-specific communication area, discarding any prior session data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Context Initialization on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the program is being accessed for the first time or as a returning session, and initializes or restores the communication area accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user returns to the Account View program with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The communication area length is greater than zero AND the entry is not a fresh navigation from the Main Menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system restores the CARDDEMO communication area from the first portion of the saved communication area, and restores the program-specific communication area from the remaining portion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Context Restoration on Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: Restores the previously saved session state from the communication area when the user is returning to the program after a prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key (ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, PF1–PF24)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the pressed key as a named indicator: ENTER maps to CCARD-AID-ENTER; CLEAR maps to CCARD-AID-CLEAR; PA1 maps to CCARD-AID-PA1; PA2 maps to CCARD-AID-PA2; PF1/PF13 map to PFK01; PF2/PF14 map to PFK02; PF3/PF15 map to PFK03; PF4/PF16 map to PFK04; PF5/PF17 map to PFK05; PF6/PF18 map to PFK06; PF7/PF19 map to PFK07; PF8/PF20 map to PFK08; PF9/PF21 map to PFK09; PF10/PF22 map to PFK10; PF11/PF23 map to PFK11; PF12/PF24 map to PFK12

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accepted Function Key Identification
all_rules.Rule_Description: Captures the function key pressed by the user and maps it to a named key indicator. Supports ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, and PF1 through PF24 (where PF13-PF24 map to PF01-PF12 equivalents).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and presses a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The pressed key is neither ENTER nor PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the key action and treats it as if the user pressed ENTER, proceeding with normal input processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unsupported Key Override to ENTER
all_rules.Rule_Description: Enforces that only ENTER and PF3 are valid user actions. Any other key press is silently overridden to behave as an ENTER key press.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3 (or PF15)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system determines the destination: if the originating transaction ID is blank or low-values, the destination transaction is set to the Main Menu transaction ID; otherwise the destination is set to the originating transaction ID. Similarly, if the originating program is blank or low-values, the destination program is set to the Main Menu program; otherwise it is set to the originating program. The current program and transaction are recorded as the 'from' context, the user type is set to USER, the program state is set to ENTER, and control is transferred to the destination program passing the updated communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Back Navigation via PF3 to Calling Program or Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3, the system navigates back to the originating program and transaction. If no originating program or transaction is recorded, the system defaults to the Main Menu.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user navigates to the Account View program for the first time (program state is ENTER)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects it is in the initial entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system builds and sends the Account View screen with no account or customer data populated, and sets the prompt-for-input message to guide the user to enter an account number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Blank Account View Screen Display on First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the first entry to the Account View program, the system displays a blank screen and prompts the user to enter an account number without any pre-populated data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the screen output area (CACTVWAO) to low-values, then populates: Title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), Title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), Transaction name (LIT-THISTRANID), Program name (LIT-THISPGM), Current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (using month digits 1-2, day digits 3-4, and year digits 3-4 of the 4-digit year), and Current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (using hours, minutes, and seconds)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population with Current Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Account View screen is displayed, the system populates the screen header with standard identification and current date/time information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered data on the Account View screen and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the user's re-entry submission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system receives the screen input into the CACTVWAI input map area, capturing the account ID field (ACCTSIDI) and any other screen fields entered by the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture User-Entered Account Number from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the data entered by the user on the Account View screen, specifically the account number field, for subsequent validation and processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user submits the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account ID field (ACCTSIDI) contains an asterisk ('*') or spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the internal account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) to low-values (blank), sets the INPUT-ERROR flag, sets the FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK flag, sets the CDEMO-ACCT-ID to zero, and if no prior error message is active, sets the prompt message to request the user to enter an account number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Blank Input Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the user has entered a value in the account number field. If the field contains an asterisk or spaces, it is treated as blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user submits the Account View screen with a non-blank account number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) is not numeric OR equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the INPUT-ERROR flag, sets the FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK flag, sets CDEMO-ACCT-ID to zero, and if no prior error message is active, displays the error message: 'Account Filter must  be a non-zero 11 digit number'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Non-Numeric or Zero Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Validates that the account number entered by the user is a numeric, non-zero value. The account number must be an 11-digit non-zero numeric value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user submits the Account View screen with an account number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The entered account ID (CC-ACCT-ID) is numeric AND not equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the entered account ID to CDEMO-ACCT-ID and sets the FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID flag to indicate the account filter is valid

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Account Number Acceptance
all_rules.Rule_Description: Accepts and stores the account number when it passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, and non-zero).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Individual account number field validation has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account filter flag is set to BLANK (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED indicator to signal that no valid search input was provided and a data lookup should not be attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Search Criteria Received Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: After individual field validation, performs a cross-field check to confirm that at least one search criterion (account number) has been provided before attempting a data lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid account ID has been entered and passed all input validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a read on the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) using the account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account is found: the associated customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) is stored in CDEMO-CUST-ID and the card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) is stored in CDEMO-CARD-NUM. If the account is not found: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the error message is set to 'Account: [account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Card Cross-Reference Lookup by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Looks up the submitted account ID in the Card Cross-Reference alternate index file (CXACAIX) to retrieve the associated customer ID and card number required for subsequent data retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account ID has been successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a read on the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) using the account ID as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record is found: the FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag is set and the full account record (ACCOUNT-RECORD) is available for display. If the account record is not found: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the error message is set to 'Account: [account ID] not found in Acct Master file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master Data Retrieval by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the full account record from the Account Master file (ACCTDAT) using the account ID, after the account has been confirmed to exist in the Cross-Reference file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a read on the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the customer ID (WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID, sourced from CDEMO-CUST-ID) as the key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the customer record is found: the FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set and the full customer record (CUSTOMER-RECORD) is available for display. If the customer record is not found: INPUT-ERROR is set, FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK is set, and the error message is set to 'CustId: [customer ID] not found in customer master. Resp: [response code] REAS: [reason code]'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Master Data Retrieval by Customer ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the full customer record from the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the customer ID obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup, after the account has been confirmed in the Account Master.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display after a data lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag OR the FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set to true
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the following account fields on the screen: Account Active Status (ACSTTUSO), Current Balance (ACURBALO), Credit Limit (ACRDLIMO), Cash Credit Limit (ACSHLIMO), Current Cycle Credit Amount (ACRCYCRO), Current Cycle Debit Amount (ACRCYDBO), Account Open Date (ADTOPENO), Account Expiration Date (AEXPDTO), Account Reissue Date (AREISDTO), and Account Group ID (AADDGRPO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Data Population on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Populates the Account View screen with account-level financial and status information when the account has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master or Customer Master file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display after a data lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set to true
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system populates the following customer fields on the screen: Customer ID (ACSTNUMO), Social Security Number formatted as XXX-XX-XXXX using characters 1-3, a dash, characters 4-5, a dash, and characters 6-9 of CUST-SSN (ACSTSSNO), FICO Credit Score (ACSTFCOO), Date of Birth in YYYY-MM-DD format (ACSTDOBO), First Name (ACSFNAMO), Middle Name (ACSMNAMO), Last Name (ACSLNAMO), Address Line 1 (ACSADL1O), Address Line 2 (ACSADL2O), City/Address Line 3 (ACSCITYO), State Code (ACSSTTEO), ZIP Code (ACSZIPCO), Country Code (ACSCTRYO), Phone Number 1 (ACSPHN1O), Phone Number 2 (ACSPHN2O), Government Issued ID (ACSGOVTO), EFT Account ID (ACSEFTCO), and Primary Card Holder Indicator (ACSPFLGO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Data Population on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Populates the Account View screen with customer personal and contact information when the customer has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file. SSN is formatted with dashes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the session is not a fresh entry (EIBCALEN is not zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account filter flag is BLANK (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the account ID display field (ACCTSIDO) to low-values. When the account filter flag is not blank, the system populates the account ID display field (ACCTSIDO) with the current account ID value (CC-ACCT-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account ID Field Display Based on Filter State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Controls how the account ID field is displayed on screen based on whether a valid account filter value exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system always: sets the account ID field to protected/secure attribute (DFHBMFSE on ACCTSIDA), positions the cursor on the account ID field (length set to -1 on ACCTSIDL), and sets the account ID field color to default (DFHDFCOL on ACCTSIDC). Additionally: if FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is true, the account ID field color is changed to RED (DFHRED). If FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is true AND the program is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), the account ID display field is set to '*' and the field color is changed to RED

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Field Attribute and Color Setup for Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: Sets the visual attributes of the Account ID field on screen, including cursor positioning and color coding to indicate validation errors.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine evaluates the informational message state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is true (no active informational message), the info message field color is set to dark/non-display (DFHBMDAR on INFOMSGC). If an informational message is active, the info message field color is set to neutral (DFHNEUTR on INFOMSGC)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Informational Message Color Display Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: Controls the display color of the informational message area on the screen based on whether an active informational message exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The INPUT-ERROR flag is set due to a validation failure (blank account, non-numeric account, zero account, or account not found in any data source)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the error message (WS-RETURN-MSG) to the screen error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), rebuilds the screen with current data and error highlighting, positions the cursor on the account ID field, highlights the account ID field in RED, and redisplays the screen to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Message Display and Screen Refresh on Validation Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When input validation fails, the system redisplays the Account View screen with the error message visible and the cursor positioned on the account ID field to guide the user to correct the input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted a valid account number that passes all input validations
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) and no INPUT-ERROR flag is set after validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system executes the account retrieval sequence in order: (1) performs the Card Cross-Reference lookup (9200-GETCARDXREF-BYACCT); if the account filter is not OK after this step, processing stops. (2) If cross-reference succeeds, performs the Account Master retrieval (9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT); if account not found, processing stops. (3) If account master succeeds, sets CDEMO-CUST-ID to WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID and performs the Customer Master retrieval (9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST). After the sequence completes, the screen is rebuilt and redisplayed with all retrieved data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account View Processing Orchestration on Valid Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: Orchestrates the complete account data retrieval sequence when the user provides a valid account number, coordinating the three-step lookup process across Cross-Reference, Account Master, and Customer Master files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen variable setup routine evaluates the message state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is true, the system sets the prompt-for-input message (WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT) to guide the user. The current return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) is always moved to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO of CACTVWAO), and the current informational message (WS-INFO-MSG) is always moved to the screen info message field (INFOMSGO of CACTVWAO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Informational Message and Prompt Management
all_rules.Rule_Description: Manages the display of informational and prompt messages on the Account View screen, ensuring the user receives appropriate guidance based on the current state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen has been sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the COMMON-RETURN point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system copies the current error/return message (WS-RETURN-MSG) to the screen error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), packages the CARDDEMO communication area into the first portion of WS-COMMAREA, packages the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) into the remaining portion of WS-COMMAREA starting after the CARDDEMO area, and issues a CICS RETURN with the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) and the fully packaged WS-COMMAREA, suspending execution until the user's next interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control with Packaged Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: Packages the complete session state into the communication area and returns control to the CICS transaction manager, preserving all context for the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user initiates the Account View program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is no communication area data available from any prior session (the session data length is zero, indicating no previous interaction exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a brand-new session with no prior context, and routes processing to perform a complete fresh initialization of all application and program-specific data areas

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect New Session - No Prior Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the program is being accessed for the very first time in a new session by checking if there is no communication area data passed from a previous interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user accesses the Account View program and prior session data exists (communication area length is non-zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The originating program is identified as the Main Menu program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals the Main Menu program identifier) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (meaning this is not a return from a previous submission on this screen)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as a new request originating from the Main Menu and routes processing to perform a complete fresh initialization, discarding any previously held session data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect New Request from Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the user has navigated to the Account View program freshly from the Main Menu without any prior re-entry flag, which also requires a clean slate initialization even when prior session data technically exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined this is either a brand-new session (no prior session data) OR a new request arriving from the Main Menu without a re-entry flag
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The fresh start initialization is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the Application Communication Area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) to its initial empty state AND resets the Program-Specific Communication Area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) to its initial empty state, ensuring the user starts with a completely clean slate with no residual data from any previous session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Start - Reset All Session Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is entered fresh (either as a brand-new session or as a new request from the Main Menu), all application-level and program-specific communication areas are fully reset to ensure no stale data from any prior session influences the current interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Account View program with an active session (prior session data exists) AND the program is NOT being accessed fresh from the Main Menu
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The re-entry restoration process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system restores the Application Communication Area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) by reading the first portion of the saved session data, exactly matching the defined length of the Application Communication Area, so that all shared application-level context from the prior interaction is fully recovered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-entry - Restore Application Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a returning user with an active session re-enters the program (e.g., after submitting an account number), the application-level communication area is restored from the previously saved session data so that shared application context (such as user type, transaction routing, and navigation history) is preserved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Account View program with an active session (prior session data exists) AND the program is NOT being accessed fresh from the Main Menu
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The re-entry restoration process is triggered after the Application Communication Area has been restored
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system restores the Program-Specific Communication Area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) by reading the second portion of the saved session data, starting immediately after the Application Communication Area's length boundary and spanning exactly the defined length of the Program-Specific Communication Area, so that all program-level context (such as previously entered account ID and screen state flags) from the prior interaction is fully recovered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-entry - Restore Program-Specific Context
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a returning user with an active session re-enters the program, the program-specific context (such as previously entered account filter values and screen state) is restored from the saved session data immediately following the application communication area, ensuring continuity of the user's prior interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and presses a function key or action key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the key press input from the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies and records the key pressed as one of the following internal key identifiers: ENTER key is recorded as CCARD-AID-ENTER; PF3 (or PF15) key is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK03; PF1 (or PF13) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK01; PF2 (or PF14) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK02; PF4 (or PF16) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK04; PF5 (or PF17) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK05; PF6 (or PF18) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK06; PF7 (or PF19) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK07; PF8 (or PF20) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK08; PF9 (or PF21) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK09; PF10 (or PF22) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK10; PF11 (or PF23) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK11; PF12 (or PF24) is recorded as CCARD-AID-PFK12; CLEAR key is recorded as CCARD-AID-CLEAR; PA1 key is recorded as CCARD-AID-PA1; PA2 key is recorded as CCARD-AID-PA2. Note: PF13-PF24 are treated as aliases for PF1-PF12 respectively.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Identify User Function Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user interacts with the Account View screen, the system must identify and record which function key was pressed. Each key press is mapped to a specific internal key identifier so the system can determine the user's intended action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has captured and identified the function key pressed by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key identification step is complete, regardless of which key was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the key validation status to INVALID as the default state, so that no key is considered valid unless it explicitly passes the subsequent validation check

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default All Key Presses to Invalid Status
all_rules.Rule_Description: After capturing the key pressed by the user, the system initially marks the key status as INVALID by default before performing any validation. This ensures that only explicitly approved keys are treated as valid actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has captured the user's key press and defaulted the key status to INVALID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the pressed key is either the ENTER key (CCARD-AID-ENTER) or the PF3 key (CCARD-AID-PFK03)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the pressed key is ENTER or PF3, the system marks the key status as VALID and proceeds with the identified key action; if the pressed key is any other key (e.g., PF1, PF2, PF4 through PF24, CLEAR, PA1, PA2), the key status remains INVALID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Accepted Function Keys - Enter and PF3 Only
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account View screen only accepts two specific function keys as valid user inputs: the ENTER key and the PF3 key. All other key presses are not recognized as valid actions for this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the pressed key and determined it is either the ENTER key or the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key is confirmed to be ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER) or PF3 (CCARD-AID-PFK03)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the key validation status to VALID (PFK-VALID = TRUE) and continues processing using the specific action associated with the identified key (ENTER for data submission or PF3 for back/exit navigation)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Valid Key Status for Accepted Keys
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses either the ENTER key or the PF3 key, the system explicitly marks the key status as VALID, allowing normal processing to continue with the specific action associated with that key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has evaluated the pressed key and determined that the key status is INVALID (i.e., the key pressed was not ENTER or PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key validation status is INVALID (PFK-INVALID = TRUE), meaning the user pressed any key other than ENTER or PF3 such as PF1, PF2, PF4-PF24, CLEAR, PA1, or PA2
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the captured key identifier and sets it to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER = TRUE), so that subsequent processing continues as if the user had pressed the ENTER key, enabling normal screen processing to proceed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Override Unsupported Key Press to ENTER Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key that is not ENTER or PF3, the system overrides the key press and treats it as if the user had pressed the ENTER key. This ensures the screen continues normal processing without interruption, regardless of unsupported key presses.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account View screen and the session communication area contains the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) is blank or empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) is set to the Main Menu Transaction (LIT-MENUTRANID); otherwise, the destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) is set to the originating transaction identifier (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Destination Transaction on PF3 Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to navigate back, the system determines which transaction to return to. If no originating transaction was recorded in the session, the system defaults to the Main Menu transaction; otherwise, it routes back to the transaction that originally called this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account View screen and the session communication area contains the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3 to navigate back
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) is blank or empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is set to the Main Menu Program (LIT-MENUPGM); otherwise, the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) is set to the originating program identifier (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Destination Program on PF3 Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: After determining the destination transaction, the system also determines which program to transfer control to. If no originating program was recorded in the session, the system defaults to the Main Menu program; otherwise, it routes back to the program that originally invoked this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination transaction (CDEMO-TO-TRANID) and destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) have been determined after the user pressed PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The communication area is updated as follows: the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) is set to the current Account View transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID); the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) is set to the current Account View program name (LIT-THISPGM); the user type (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER) is set to standard User; the program entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER) is marked as Fresh Entry; the last visited mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET) is set to the current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET); and the last visited map (CDEMO-LAST-MAP) is set to the current map (LIT-THISMAP)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Communication Area with Current Program Context Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system updates the shared communication area to record the Account View program and transaction as the originating source, sets the user type to standard User, marks the program state as a Fresh Entry (not a re-entry), and records the current map and mapset as the last visited screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been determined and the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has been updated with the current program context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the navigation transfer on PF3 press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program identified in CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, and the full updated communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is passed to the receiving program so it has complete session and navigation context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Program with Updated Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: After updating the communication area with the current program context, the system transfers control to the resolved destination program, passing the full updated communication area so the receiving program has complete session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user initiates the Account View program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is no prior session communication area (EIBCALEN equals zero), OR the program was called from the Main Menu program and the re-entry flag is not set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system treats this as a fresh entry: all shared application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) are fully initialized to their default empty state, discarding any prior session data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Fresh Program Entry and Initialize Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether the Account View program is being accessed for the first time (fresh entry) — either because no prior session exists or because the user navigated from the Main Menu without re-entering — and initializes all session data accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (1100-SCREEN-INIT) is invoked as part of the send-map process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All fields in the Account View screen output area (CACTVWAO) are set to low values, effectively blanking the entire screen before any new data is populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Output Fields Before Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the Account View screen with any data, all screen output fields must be cleared to ensure no residual data from a previous interaction is inadvertently displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is initializing the Account View screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen initialization routine (1100-SCREEN-INIT) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: (1) Application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) in the TITLE01O field, (2) Application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) in the TITLE02O field, (3) The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) in the TRNNAMEO field, (4) The current program name (LIT-THISPGM) in the PGMNAMEO field, (5) The current system date formatted as MM/DD/YY in the CURDATEO field, and (6) The current system time formatted as HH:MM:SS in the CURTIMEO field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Application Identity and Current Date/Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Account View screen is displayed, the screen header must be populated with the application titles, the current transaction ID, the current program name, and the real-time current date and time to provide the user with context and orientation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is setting up the screen variables for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The communication area length (EIBCALEN) equals zero, indicating no prior session exists
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the display mode flag to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT (true), which causes all account data fields and customer data fields on the screen to remain blank — no account status, balances, credit limits, dates, customer name, address, or any other account/customer information is shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Prompt-for-Input Mode on Fresh Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account View screen is being displayed for the first time with no prior session data, the system must set the display mode to 'prompt for input' so that no account or customer data fields are populated and the user is guided to enter an account number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is finalizing screen variable setup for the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is true (no informational message has been set by prior processing)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system re-sets the display mode to WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT (true); the current return/error message (WS-RETURN-MSG) is moved to the screen error message field (ERRMSGO), and the current informational message (WS-INFO-MSG — which contains the prompt 'Enter or update id of account to display') is moved to the screen informational message field (INFOMSGO) for display to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Input Prompt Message When No Account Data is Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is in prompt-for-input mode (no account data to display), the informational message area must show a prompt guiding the user to enter an account ID. Additionally, if no informational message is available, the prompt-for-input mode is re-enforced.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is setting screen display attributes for the Account View screen prior to sending it to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup routine (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) is executed for a fresh entry with no validation errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system: (1) Sets the Account ID field (ACCTSIDA) to protected/secure attribute (DFHBMFSE), (2) Sets the cursor length indicator (ACCTSIDL) to -1 to position the cursor on the Account ID field regardless of filter status, (3) Sets the Account ID field color (ACCTSIDC) to the default color (DFHDFCOL) — no red highlighting since there are no errors, and (4) Sets the informational message field color (INFOMSGC) to dark/suppressed (DFHBMDAR) if no informational message is present, or to neutral color (DFHNEUTR) if an informational message exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Position Cursor on Account ID Field and Apply Default Field Colors
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the initial blank Account View screen, the cursor must be positioned on the Account ID input field to guide the user, the field must be set to its default color (no error highlighting), and the informational message area color must reflect whether a message is present.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen has been fully initialized with header, blank data fields, prompt message, cursor position, and field colors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The send-screen routine (1400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system: (1) Records the current map name (LIT-THISMAP) and mapset name (LIT-THISMAPSET) as the next map/mapset to be used, (2) Sets the program state flag to CDEMO-PGM-REENTER (true) so the next user interaction will be treated as a re-entry/data submission, (3) Sends the Account View screen (CACTVWAO) to the user's terminal with the screen fully erased (ERASE) and the keyboard unlocked (FREEKB), with the cursor positioned on the Account ID field (CURSOR)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Blank Account View Screen and Mark Session for Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen fields and attributes have been prepared, the Account View screen must be sent to the user's terminal with the screen cleared and the keyboard unlocked. The session state must be updated to 're-entry' mode so that the next user interaction is processed as a data submission.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View program has been entered and the session has been identified as a first-time (fresh) entry with the program state set to CDEMO-PGM-ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main program logic evaluates the program state as CDEMO-PGM-ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system invokes the full send-map sequence (1000-SEND-MAP through 1000-SEND-MAP-EXIT), which in turn executes: screen initialization (1100-SCREEN-INIT), screen variable setup (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS), screen attribute setup (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS), and screen transmission (1400-SEND-SCREEN); after which control is passed to COMMON-RETURN to save session state and await the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Screen Display Sequence on First Program Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account View program is entered for the first time (program-enter state), the system must invoke the complete screen preparation and display sequence — covering initialization, variable setup, attribute setup, and screen transmission — before returning control to await user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is about to be prepared for display to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header initialization process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen output fields on the Account View screen (CACTVWAO) must be cleared and reset to blank/low values before any new data is populated, ensuring a clean slate for the new screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Screen Output Fields Before Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the Account View screen header with any data, all screen output fields must be reset to a blank/empty state to ensure no residual data from a previous display is shown to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen header initialization is in progress and all screen fields have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system needs to populate the date and time fields on the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current system date and time must be retrieved using the system's current date function and stored in the working storage date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must retrieve the current date and time from the operating system to display accurate, real-time information on the Account View screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen header initialization is in progress
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The application title section of the screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Title Line 1 (TITLE01O) on the screen header must be populated with the first application title (CCDA-TITLE01), and Title Line 2 (TITLE02O) on the screen header must be populated with the second application title (CCDA-TITLE02)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Title Lines on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account View screen header must display two lines of application title text to identify the application to the user. Both title lines are sourced from the application's standard title definitions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen header initialization is in progress and application titles have been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction identification section of the screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen header must be populated with the current transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) assigned to this Account View program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account View screen header must display the current transaction identifier so the user can identify which transaction they are working within.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen header initialization is in progress and the Transaction ID has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program identification section of the screen header is being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Program Name field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen header must be populated with the current program name (LIT-THISPGM) of the Account View program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account View screen header must display the current program name so the user and support staff can identify which program is currently executing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system date is being formatted for display on the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) must be extracted into WS-CURDATE-MM, the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) must be extracted into WS-CURDATE-DD, and only the last 2 digits of the year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) must be extracted into WS-CURDATE-YY, resulting in a combined date value in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY formatted as MM/DD/YY

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current System Date as MM/DD/YY
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system date retrieved from the operating system must be decomposed into its individual components (month, day, year) and formatted into the standard MM/DD/YY display format for the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date is being placed onto the screen header for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted date value (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) in MM/DD/YY format must be moved to the Current Date display field (CURDATEO) on the Account View screen header (CACTVWAO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Formatted Date on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted system date in MM/DD/YY format must be displayed in the designated date field on the Account View screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date and time have been retrieved and stored in WS-CURDATE-DATA, which also contains the time components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system time is being formatted for display on the screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) must be extracted into WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) must be extracted into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) must be extracted into WS-CURTIME-SS, resulting in a combined time value in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS formatted as HH:MM:SS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current System Time as HH:MM:SS
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current system time must be decomposed into its individual components (hours, minutes, seconds) and formatted into the standard HH:MM:SS display format for the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format and stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The time is being placed onto the screen header for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted time value (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) in HH:MM:SS format must be moved to the Current Time display field (CURTIMEO) on the Account View screen header (CACTVWAO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Formatted Time on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted system time in HH:MM:SS format must be displayed in the designated time field on the Account View screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted an Account ID for lookup and the system has attempted to retrieve data from the Account Master file and the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the account record was found in the Account Master file OR the customer record was found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If at least one of the two records (Account Master or Customer Master) was successfully retrieved, the system proceeds to populate all account details on the screen. If neither record was found, the system skips account data population and no account details are displayed on the screen.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Eligibility to Populate Account Data on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system determines whether account data should be displayed on the Account View screen based on whether account or customer records were successfully retrieved from their respective master files.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Active Status field on the screen is populated with the active status value retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Active Status on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's active status on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Balance field on the screen is populated with the current balance value retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Balance on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's current balance on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit field on the screen is populated with the credit limit value retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Credit Limit on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's total credit limit on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cash Credit Limit field on the screen is populated with the cash credit limit value retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Cash Credit Limit on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's cash credit limit on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Credit field on the screen is populated with the current cycle credit amount retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Cycle Credit on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's current billing cycle credit amount on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Current Cycle Debit field on the screen is populated with the current cycle debit amount retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Current Cycle Debit on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's current billing cycle debit amount on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Open Date field on the screen is populated with the account open date retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Open Date on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the date the account was opened on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Expiration Date field on the screen is populated with the expiration date retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Expiration Date on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's expiration date on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Reissue Date field on the screen is populated with the reissue date retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Account Reissue Date on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's most recent reissue date on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file OR the customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with account details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Group ID field on the screen is populated with the account group identifier retrieved from the Account Master record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Group ID on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data is available, the system displays the account's group identifier on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to retrieve data from both the Account Master file and the Customer Master file for the submitted Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record was NOT found in the Account Master file AND the customer record was NOT found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the population of all account detail fields on the screen. No account status, balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, cycle credit, cycle debit, open date, expiration date, reissue date, or group ID is displayed.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Account Data Population When No Records Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither the account record nor the customer record was successfully retrieved, the system skips all account data population and leaves account detail fields blank on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted a valid Account ID on the Account View screen and the system has completed the account lookup process
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the customer record was successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the customer record was found (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is set to TRUE), the system proceeds to populate all customer-related fields on the screen; if the customer record was NOT found, all customer-related fields on the screen remain blank (empty)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Data Retrieval Gate Check
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determines whether customer data should be populated on the Account View screen based on whether the customer record was successfully found in the Customer Master file during the account lookup process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID (CUST-ID) is displayed in the Customer Number field (ACSTNUMO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer ID on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the unique Customer ID on the Account View screen so the user can identify the customer associated with the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE) and the raw SSN (CUST-SSN) is stored as a 9-digit value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the SSN for display on the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The SSN is formatted by concatenating the first 3 digits of CUST-SSN, followed by a dash '-', followed by digits 4 and 5 of CUST-SSN, followed by a dash '-', followed by digits 6 through 9 of CUST-SSN, and the resulting formatted value (e.g., 123-45-6789) is displayed in the SSN field (ACSTSSNO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Customer SSN in Masked Dash-Separated Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system formats the customer's Social Security Number into the standard XXX-XX-XXXX display format by inserting dashes between the SSN segments before displaying it on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's FICO Credit Score (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE) is displayed in the FICO score field (ACSTFCOO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer FICO Credit Score on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's FICO credit score on the Account View screen to provide the user with the customer's creditworthiness indicator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's Date of Birth (CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD) is displayed in the date of birth field (ACSTDOBO) on the Account View screen in YYYY-MM-DD format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Date of Birth on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's date of birth on the Account View screen in YYYY-MM-DD format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME) is displayed in the first name field (ACSFNAMO), the customer's Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME) is displayed in the middle name field (ACSMNAMO), and the customer's Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME) is displayed in the last name field (ACSLNAMO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Full Name on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's complete name — first name, middle name, and last name — as separate fields on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's Address Line 1 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-1) is displayed in the address line 1 field (ACSADL1O) and the customer's Address Line 2 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-2) is displayed in the address line 2 field (ACSADL2O) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Address Lines on Account View Screen
