all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's street address lines on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's City (CUST-ADDR-LINE-3) is displayed in the city field (ACSCITYO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer City on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's city of residence on the Account View screen. The city value is sourced from the third address line of the customer record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's State Code (CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD) is displayed in the state field (ACSSTTEO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer State Code on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's state code on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's Zip Code (CUST-ADDR-ZIP) is displayed in the zip code field (ACSZIPCO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Zip Code on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's postal zip code on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's Country Code (CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD) is displayed in the country field (ACSCTRYO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Country Code on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's country code on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's primary Phone Number (CUST-PHONE-NUM-1) is displayed in the phone number 1 field (ACSPHN1O) and the customer's secondary Phone Number (CUST-PHONE-NUM-2) is displayed in the phone number 2 field (ACSPHN2O) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Phone Numbers on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays both of the customer's phone numbers on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's Government-Issued ID (CUST-GOVT-ISSUED-ID) is displayed in the government ID field (ACSGOVTO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer Government-Issued ID on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's government-issued identification number on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's EFT Account ID (CUST-EFT-ACCOUNT-ID) is displayed in the EFT account field (ACSEFTCO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Customer EFT Account ID on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the customer's Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) account identifier on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the Account View screen with customer information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The customer's Primary Card Holder Indicator (CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND) is displayed in the primary card holder flag field (ACSPFLGO) on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Primary Card Holder Indicator on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When customer data has been successfully retrieved, the system displays the indicator that identifies whether the customer is the primary card holder for the account on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account lookup process has completed but the customer record was NOT found in the Customer Master file (FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag is NOT set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the Account View screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All customer-related fields on the screen (Customer ID, SSN, FICO Score, Date of Birth, First/Middle/Last Name, Address Lines, City, State, Zip Code, Country, Phone Numbers, Government-Issued ID, EFT Account ID, and Primary Card Holder Indicator) remain blank as initialized, and no customer data population steps are executed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Customer Data Section When Customer Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the customer record was not successfully retrieved from the Customer Master file, the system skips the entire customer data population section, leaving all customer-related fields on the Account View screen blank.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen field attributes are being set up, regardless of whether the Account ID is valid, invalid, or blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The cursor must be placed on the Account ID input field so that the user can immediately begin entering or correcting the Account ID without manually navigating to the field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning on Account ID Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor must always be positioned on the Account ID input field when the Account View screen is displayed, regardless of the validation status of the account ID. This ensures the user's focus is directed to the primary input field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen field attributes are being initialized for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID field color is being set up prior to any validation-based color overrides
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID field must be displayed in the default system color as the baseline presentation, which may subsequently be overridden to red if a validation error is detected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Color Applied to Account ID Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID field on the Account View screen is initially assigned the default display color as a baseline before any conditional color overrides are applied based on validation results.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Account View screen with an Account ID value that has failed validation (the account ID is flagged as not valid — either non-numeric or zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field attributes are being configured for the re-displayed screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID field must be highlighted in RED color to visually indicate to the user that the entered Account ID is invalid and must be corrected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Red Highlight on Account ID Field for Invalid Account Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID entered by the user fails validation (e.g., non-numeric value or zero value), the Account ID field must be visually highlighted in red to alert the user that the entered value is not acceptable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has previously visited the Account View screen (it is a re-entry, not a first-time display) AND the Account ID field has been left blank (empty, spaces, or containing only an asterisk)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen field attributes are being configured for the re-displayed screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID field must display an asterisk character ('*') as a visual placeholder marker AND the field must be highlighted in RED color to indicate to the user that an Account ID is required and was not provided

all_rules.Rule_Name: Asterisk Marker and Red Highlight for Blank Account ID on Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user re-submits the Account View screen without providing an Account ID (leaving the field blank), the system must place an asterisk marker in the Account ID field and highlight it in red to clearly indicate that the Account ID is a required field that was not provided.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is no informational message available to present to the user (the informational message indicator is set to 'no message')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message display area must be rendered in a dimmed or dark color to visually communicate to the user that no active informational message is present

all_rules.Rule_Name: Dimmed Display Color for Informational Message Area When No Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When there is no active informational message to display to the user, the informational message area on the Account View screen must be rendered in a dimmed or dark color to visually indicate that the area is inactive and contains no relevant information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An informational message is available and needs to be presented to the user (the informational message indicator is set to 'message present')
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message display area must be rendered in a neutral color to ensure the active informational message is clearly visible and legible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Neutral Display Color for Informational Message Area When Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an active informational message is available to display to the user, the informational message area on the Account View screen must be rendered in a neutral color to ensure the message is clearly visible and readable.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has navigated to the Account View screen and the program is being invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the current program state flag (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER for first entry vs CDEMO-PGM-REENTER for subsequent interaction)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the program state is FIRST ENTRY (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER), the system bypasses all input capture and proceeds directly to display a fresh Account View screen. If the program state is RE-ENTRY (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), the system proceeds to capture and process the user-submitted input from the screen.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether to Capture User Input Based on Program Entry State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system determines whether the user has previously interacted with the Account View screen. Only when the program is in a re-entry state (user has already seen the screen and submitted data) should the system attempt to capture and process user input. On first entry, no input capture occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in a re-entry state, meaning the user has previously been presented with the Account View screen and has pressed ENTER to submit their input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the screen map data from the Account View screen (map: CACTVWAI)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All user-entered data from the Account View screen is captured into the program's input working area (CACTVWAI), making it available for subsequent retrieval and validation steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture User Input from Account View Screen on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user has submitted the Account View screen, the system captures all data entered by the user from the Account View screen map (CACTVWAI) into the working input area for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's screen input has been captured from the Account View screen into the input working area (CACTVWAI)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the Account ID input field (ACCTSIDI) from the captured screen data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account ID field contains an asterisk ('*') or spaces, the account number (CC-ACCT-ID) is set to empty (LOW-VALUES), indicating no account number was provided. If the Account ID field contains any other value, that value is stored as the account number (CC-ACCT-ID) to be passed forward for validation.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Number Entered by User from Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: After capturing the screen input, the system retrieves the account number value entered by the user. If the user entered an asterisk ('*') or left the field blank (spaces), the account number is treated as not provided. Otherwise, the entered value is stored as the account number to be validated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user's account number input has been retrieved from the Account View screen and stored in the working area (CC-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The input processing sequence completes the capture phase (2100-RECEIVE-MAP) and moves to the edit/validation phase (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The captured input is passed to the validation process (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS). The current program name (LIT-THISPGM), mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET), and map name (LIT-THISMAP) are recorded in the screen control area (CCARD-NEXT-PROG, CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET, CCARD-NEXT-MAP) to support subsequent screen redisplay. Any return message is also carried forward (WS-RETURN-MSG to CCARD-ERROR-MSG).

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pass Captured Account Input for Validation Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the account number has been retrieved from the screen input, the system passes the captured input through the validation process. The sequence ensures that input capture always precedes validation, and the current program context (program name, map, mapset) is recorded for screen redisplay purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been invoked and the program state indicates this is the first time the user is entering the Account View screen (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER state)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the program entry state and determines it is a first-time entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips all input capture and validation steps entirely, proceeds directly to build and send the Account View screen (1000-SEND-MAP), and returns control to wait for the user's first interaction. No account data lookup is performed.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Fresh Account View Screen on First Program Entry Without Input Capture
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Account View screen for the first time (first program entry), the system does not attempt to capture or process any user input. Instead, it immediately displays a blank Account View screen prompting the user to enter an account number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and has submitted the Account Number input field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Number field contains an asterisk ('*') or only spaces
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Number is treated as blank (cleared to empty/low values) and is considered not provided, so that subsequent blank validation rules are triggered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Normalize Account Number Input - Treat Asterisk or Spaces as Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validating the account number, any entry of an asterisk ('*') or spaces in the Account Number field is treated as if no account number was provided, normalizing the input to a blank/empty value for downstream validation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and submits the form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Number field is blank, empty, or contains only spaces (including when normalized from asterisk or spaces)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error flag is set, the Account Number filter is marked as blank, the stored Account ID is cleared to zero, and the user is prompted with a message to provide an Account Number; no account lookup is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Blank or Not Provided - Mandatory Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Number is a mandatory input field. If the user submits the screen without entering an Account Number (field is empty or blank), an error must be raised and the user must be prompted to provide an Account Number before any account lookup can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen, has provided a non-blank Account Number, and submits the form
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Number contains non-numeric characters OR the Account Number equals zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An input error flag is set, the Account Number filter is marked as invalid, the stored Account ID is cleared to zero, and the error message 'Account Filter must be a non-zero 11 digit number' is displayed to the user; no account lookup is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Non-Numeric or Zero - Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Number must be a numeric, non-zero value. If the user enters a value that contains non-numeric characters or is equal to zero, an error must be raised with a specific message indicating the required format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Account View screen and submits the form with an Account Number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Number is non-blank, is fully numeric, and is not equal to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Number is stored as the Account ID for further processing and the Account Number filter status is marked as valid, allowing the account lookup to proceed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Valid Account Number - Store for Further Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Number passes all validation checks (non-blank, numeric, and non-zero), it is accepted as a valid input, stored for account lookup processing, and the Account Number filter is marked as valid to allow the account retrieval process to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Account Number input validation has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Number filter is marked as blank (no account number was provided by the user)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system additionally sets a flag indicating that no search criteria were received, confirming that account lookup cannot be initiated

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Search Criteria Received - Blank Account Filter Post-Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After account number validation, if the Account Number filter is determined to be blank, the system must additionally flag that no search criteria were received. This ensures the overall input processing correctly reflects that the user did not supply any searchable account information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The individual account field validation has completed and the Account Filter Flag has been marked as Blank (meaning the user submitted the screen without entering an Account ID — the field was empty, contained only spaces, or contained '*')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The cross-field validation check evaluates whether the Account Filter Blank flag is active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the 'No Search Criteria Received' condition to TRUE, indicating that the user provided no input to search on, and no account data lookup is initiated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Missing Account Search Criteria After Field Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After individual account field validation completes, the system performs a cross-field check to determine whether the account filter was left blank. If no account number was provided by the user, the system sets a 'No Search Criteria Received' condition to prevent any data lookup from proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Account View screen with the Account ID field left empty (blank, spaces, or containing '*'), and no error or return message has been previously set during the current interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account field validation detects that the Account ID is equal to LOW-VALUES or SPACES (i.e., the Account Filter Blank flag is set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the prompt message to 'Enter account number to display' (WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT), marks the input as an error (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE), sets the Account Filter Flag to Blank, and clears the Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero — no account data lookup is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prompt User to Enter Account Number When Field Is Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID field is found to be blank during individual field validation, and no prior error message has already been set in the session, the system sets a prompt message instructing the user to enter an account number. This prompt guides the user on the required action to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a valid Account ID that has passed all input validations (non-blank, numeric, non-zero, 11-digit)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the account data retrieval process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the validated Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) as the search key (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID) to perform a lookup against the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX alternate index)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Account ID as Search Key for Cross-Reference Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an account view request, the system must use the validated Account ID entered by the user as the key to search the Card Cross-Reference file to retrieve associated customer and card information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is found successfully in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must retrieve the Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) from the cross-reference record and store it as the active Customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) for use in the subsequent Customer Master lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer ID from Card Cross-Reference on Successful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account ID is successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must retrieve and store the associated Customer ID for use in subsequent customer data retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) and the account has been found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is found successfully in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must retrieve the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) from the cross-reference record and store it as the active Card Number (CDEMO-CARD-NUM) for the current session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Card Number from Card Cross-Reference on Successful Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account ID is successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must also retrieve and store the associated Card Number linked to that account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup of the Account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is NOT found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the input state to error (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE) and mark the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), preventing any further account or customer data retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Account Filter as Invalid When Account Not Found in Cross-Reference
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the entered Account ID cannot be located in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must flag the account filter as invalid and mark the overall input as an error to prevent further data retrieval processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file (CXACAIX) has failed because the account was not found, and no prior error message has been set for the current transaction (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the account not-found condition from the Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must build an error message in the format: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [Response Code] Reas: [Reason Code]' and store it in WS-RETURN-MSG to be displayed to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Account Not Found Error Message for Cross-Reference Lookup Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must construct and display a specific error message identifying the account that was searched and indicating it was not found in the cross-reference file, but only if no prior error message has already been set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has failed and the account filter has been marked as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue with Account Master and Customer Master lookups
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately stop all further data retrieval processing (skip Account Master lookup and Customer Master lookup) and proceed directly to display the error message to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Account Data Retrieval Processing When Cross-Reference Lookup Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the account filter has been marked as invalid, the system must immediately stop all further account and customer data retrieval and return to display the error to the user without proceeding to Account Master or Customer Master lookups.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid, non-zero, 11-digit numeric Account ID has passed all input validations and has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full account record from the Account Master File into the Account Record data area, making all account details available for further processing and screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Lookup by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an account view request, the system must retrieve full account details from the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the submitted Account ID as the search key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the submitted Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Master File lookup returns a successful match — the account record exists in the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the account as found (FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag is set to TRUE), making all retrieved account details — including Account Status, Current Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Current Cycle Credit, Current Cycle Debit, Open Date, Expiration Date, Reissue Date, and Group ID — available for display on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Found in Account Master - Mark Account as Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup successfully locates the account record, the system must flag the account as found so that all retrieved account details are made available for display on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup on the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) using the submitted Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account Master File lookup finds no matching account record for the submitted Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the overall Input Error flag (INPUT-ERROR = TRUE) and marks the Account ID field filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK = TRUE), stopping any further data retrieval (Customer Master lookup is not performed)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found in Account Master - Set Error Indicator on Account ID Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup fails to locate the submitted Account ID, the system must flag the input as invalid and mark the Account ID field as erroneous to prevent further data retrieval and to trigger error display on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File (ACCTDAT) lookup has returned a 'not found' result for the submitted Account ID, and no prior error message has already been set for this transaction (WS-RETURN-MSG is currently OFF/empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the account does not exist in the Account Master File and that no earlier error message has been recorded
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system builds and stores an error message in the format: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Acct Master file' — this message is then displayed on the Account View screen to inform the user that the entered Account ID does not exist in the Account Master File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Not Found in Account Master - Build User-Facing Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Master File lookup fails to locate the submitted Account ID and no prior error message has been set, the system must construct and display a descriptive error message identifying the specific Account ID that was not found in the Account Master File.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account lookup has been successfully completed against the Card Cross-Reference file, and a Customer ID has been retrieved and stored from that cross-reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to retrieve customer details from the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup as the search key to query the Customer Master file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer ID Source for Master File Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID used to search the Customer Master file must be the one retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file during the earlier account lookup step, not a user-entered value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Customer ID has been obtained from the Card Cross-Reference file and is ready to be used as a search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a lookup against the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the complete customer record associated with that Customer ID from the Customer Master file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Master File Read Operation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must perform a direct lookup against the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) using the Customer ID as the unique identifier to retrieve the full customer record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup against the Customer Master file using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Master file returns a matching customer record successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the customer as found (set FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag to TRUE), making all retrieved customer details available for display on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Found - Mark for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record is successfully located in the Customer Master file, the system must flag the customer as found so that all customer details are made available for display on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup against the Customer Master file using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference, and no prior error message has been set for this transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Master file does not contain a record matching the provided Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must generate an error message in the format: 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master' and store it as the return message to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Not Found - Error Message Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference cannot be located in the Customer Master file, the system must generate a specific error message identifying the missing Customer ID to inform the user that the customer record does not exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has performed a lookup against the Customer Master file using the Customer ID from the Card Cross-Reference
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Master file does not contain a record matching the provided Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the INPUT-ERROR flag to TRUE, set the customer filter status to invalid (FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK), and immediately stop all further account data retrieval processing by exiting the account read orchestration routine

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Not Found - Flag Input as Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer record cannot be found in the Customer Master file, the system must flag the overall transaction as an input error and mark the customer filter as invalid, preventing any further data retrieval or processing steps from executing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master file lookup has returned a 'not found' result for the given Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to set the 'customer not found' error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must only write the error message 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master' if the return message flag is currently in the OFF state (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE), ensuring that any previously set error message is not overwritten

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Message Overwrite Prevention
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer is not found in the Customer Master file, the system must only set the error message if no prior error message has already been recorded for this transaction, preventing overwriting of earlier, potentially more relevant error messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted a valid Account ID for viewing account details
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account view processing sequence is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Any existing informational message is cleared, and the submitted Account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is set as the lookup key (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID) to be used in the subsequent cross-reference file search

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Account View Processing State
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before initiating the account retrieval sequence, the system clears any previously displayed informational messages and prepares the submitted Account ID as the lookup key for the cross-reference search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has been prepared as the lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the Card Cross-Reference file using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to retrieve the cross-reference record that links the Account ID to a Customer ID and Card Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Look Up Account in Card Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first step in the account retrieval sequence is to search the Card Cross-Reference file using the submitted Account ID to establish the link between the account and its associated customer and card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID has been submitted for lookup and the Card Cross-Reference file has been searched
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The associated Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) is stored as CDEMO-CUST-ID and the associated Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) is stored as CDEMO-CARD-NUM for use in subsequent processing steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer ID and Card Number from Cross-Reference
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID is successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system extracts the associated Customer ID and Card Number to be used in subsequent lookup steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted an Account ID and the system has searched the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input as an error (INPUT-ERROR), marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), and if no prior error message exists, constructs an error message in the format: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Cross ref file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]', and all further account and customer data retrieval steps are stopped

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Account Not Found in Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the submitted Account ID cannot be located in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system flags the account filter as invalid, generates a descriptive error message identifying the missing account, and halts all further data retrieval processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID has been successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the associated Customer ID and Card Number have been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the Account Master file using the Account ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to retrieve the complete account record containing account status, balances, limits, and dates from the Account Master file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Details from Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second step in the account retrieval sequence retrieves the full account record from the Account Master file using the Account ID, only executed after a successful cross-reference lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the Account Master file using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is found in the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the FOUND-ACCT-IN-MASTER flag to TRUE, indicating that account data (status, balances, credit limits, dates, group ID) is available and should be displayed on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Account Data as Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account record is successfully found in the Account Master file, the system sets a flag to indicate that account data is available for display on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the system has searched the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID is not found in the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input as an error (INPUT-ERROR), marks the account filter as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK), and if no prior error message exists, constructs an error message in the format: 'Account: [Account ID] not found in Acct Master file. Resp: [response code] Reas: [reason code]', and all further customer data retrieval steps are stopped

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Account Not Found in Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account ID exists in the Cross-Reference file but cannot be located in the Account Master file, the system flags the account filter as invalid, generates a descriptive error message, and halts all further data retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID has been found in both the Card Cross-Reference file and the Account Master file, and the Customer ID (CDEMO-CUST-ID) was retrieved from the Cross-Reference file in Step 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system searches the Customer Master file using the Customer ID (WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID) as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts to retrieve the complete customer record containing personal details, address, contact information, and financial identifiers from the Customer Master file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer Details from Customer Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The third and final step in the account retrieval sequence retrieves the full customer record from the Customer Master file using the Customer ID obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup in Step 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has searched the Customer Master file using the Customer ID obtained from the Cross-Reference lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The customer record is found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the FOUND-CUST-IN-MASTER flag to TRUE, indicating that customer data (name, SSN, date of birth, FICO score, address, phone numbers, government ID, EFT account ID, primary card holder indicator) is available and should be displayed on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Customer Data as Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the customer record is successfully found in the Customer Master file, the system sets a flag to indicate that customer data is available for display on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID was found in both the Cross-Reference and Account Master files, and the system has searched the Customer Master file using the associated Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer ID is not found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the input as an error (INPUT-ERROR), marks the customer filter as invalid (FLG-CUSTFILTER-NOT-OK), and if no prior error message exists, constructs an error message in the format: 'CustId: [Customer ID] not found in customer master. Resp: [response code] REAS: [reason code]', and processing stops

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Customer Not Found in Customer Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer ID linked to the account cannot be located in the Customer Master file, the system flags the customer filter as invalid, generates a descriptive error message identifying the missing customer, and halts processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has been submitted by the user and passed all input validation checks
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the account data retrieval sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must execute the three retrieval steps in strict order: (1) Card Cross-Reference lookup, (2) Account Master retrieval, (3) Customer Master retrieval. If Step 1 fails (account not found in cross-reference or FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set), Steps 2 and 3 are skipped entirely. If Step 2 fails (account not found in Account Master), Step 3 is skipped entirely. Only if all three steps succeed are all account and customer details available for display. Any failure at any step results in an error message being displayed to the user with no partial data retrieval continuing beyond the failed step.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Sequential Three-Step Account Data Retrieval with Stop-on-Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account view processing must follow a strict sequential order: Cross-Reference lookup first, then Account Master retrieval, then Customer Master retrieval. If any step fails, all subsequent steps are skipped and the error is surfaced to the user immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account View screen and the Account ID input field (ACCTSIDI) contains spaces, an asterisk '*', or is otherwise empty (LOW-VALUES), resulting in CC-ACCT-ID being set to LOW-VALUES
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs input validation on the submitted Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the INPUT-ERROR flag to TRUE, (2) Set the FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK flag to TRUE, (3) If no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE), set the prompt message WS-RETURN-MSG to prompt the user to enter an account number (WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT), (4) Clear the internal account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zeros, and (5) Stop further account validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Blank Account Number Error Detection and Message Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user submits the Account View screen without entering an Account ID (field is empty, spaces, or contains only an asterisk placeholder), the system must detect the blank condition, flag it, and set a prompt message instructing the user to provide an account number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Account View screen and has entered a value in the Account ID field that is either non-numeric (contains letters or special characters) or is numerically equal to zero (all zeros)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs input validation on the submitted Account ID after confirming it is not blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Set the INPUT-ERROR flag to TRUE, (2) Set the FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK flag to TRUE, (3) If no prior error message has been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE), set the error message WS-RETURN-MSG to 'Account Filter must be a non-zero 11 digit number', (4) Clear the internal account ID (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) to zero, and (5) Stop further account validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Non-Numeric or Zero Account Number Error Detection and Message Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters an Account ID that contains non-numeric characters or is entirely zeros, the system must detect the invalid format, flag the error, and display a specific error message indicating the required format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user submits the Account View screen and the account ID field is blank, resulting in FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK being set to TRUE during account validation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the map input editing process (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS) after account validation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED status flag to TRUE, indicating that the user provided no account search criteria at all

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Search Criteria Received Status Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account ID field is blank and no search criteria has been provided by the user, the system must set a specific status indicator to communicate that no search criteria was received, distinguishing this condition from other types of input errors.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input validation has completed and an error condition exists (INPUT-ERROR is TRUE), with an error message stored in WS-RETURN-MSG
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the Account View screen after a validation failure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must move the contents of WS-RETURN-MSG to the screen error message output field CCARD-ERROR-MSG (ERRMSGO of CACTVWAO), making the error message visible to the user on the refreshed screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Message Propagation to Screen Display Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: After input validation errors are detected, the system must transfer the error message from the internal working storage message field to the screen's designated error message display area so it is visible to the user on the refreshed screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing screen attributes for the Account View screen after a validation error, where either FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE, FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is TRUE, or any other condition applies
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up screen display attributes in the screen attribute setup process (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the cursor length indicator for the Account ID field (ACCTSIDL of CACTVWAI) to -1 in all cases, which positions the cursor on the Account ID input field regardless of the specific error type encountered

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning on Account ID Field for Error Correction
all_rules.Rule_Description: Whenever the Account View screen is displayed after a validation error — regardless of whether the account ID was blank or contained an invalid value — the system must always position the cursor on the Account ID input field to guide the user directly to the field requiring correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has previously submitted the Account View screen (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE) and the Account ID field was blank (FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up screen display attributes for the Account View screen refresh
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Display an asterisk character '*' in the Account ID output field (ACCTSIDO of CACTVWAO) as a visual placeholder, and (2) Set the color of the Account ID field (ACCTSIDC of CACTVWAO) to RED (DFHRED) to visually alert the user that the field requires a valid account number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Blank Account ID Field Highlighted Red with Asterisk Placeholder on Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user re-enters the Account View screen (after a prior submission) with a blank Account ID field, the system must visually highlight the Account ID field in red and display an asterisk as a placeholder to clearly indicate to the user that the field requires input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered an Account ID value that failed validation, resulting in FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK being set to TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up screen display attributes for the Account View screen refresh
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the color attribute of the Account ID field (ACCTSIDC of CACTVWAO) to RED (DFHRED), visually signaling to the user that the entered account number is invalid and requires correction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Account ID Field Highlighted Red
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters an Account ID value that fails validation (non-numeric or zero), the system must highlight the Account ID field in red on the refreshed screen to visually indicate to the user that the entered value is invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing screen display attributes for the Account View screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether an informational message is available (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag status)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is TRUE (no informational message available), the system must set the information message area color (INFOMSGC of CACTVWAO) to dark (DFHBMDAR); otherwise, if an informational message is available, the system must set the information message area color to neutral (DFHNEUTR)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Information Message Area Color Based on Message Availability
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must control the visual appearance of the information message area on the Account View screen based on whether an informational message is available to display, using dark color when no message exists and neutral color when a message is present.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed preparing all screen content, error messages, field highlights, and cursor positioning for the Account View screen after a validation error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the screen send operation (1400-SEND-SCREEN) using the configured map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and mapset (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Mark the session as a re-entry (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER set to TRUE) so the next user submission is processed as a correction attempt, (2) Send the Account View screen (CACTVWAO) to the user's terminal with the CURSOR option to position the cursor on the Account ID field, (3) Erase the previous screen content (ERASE), and (4) Unlock the keyboard (FREEKB) so the user can immediately type corrections

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account View Screen Refresh and Display with Error Highlights
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all error messages and screen attributes have been prepared, the system must send the Account View screen to the user with all error highlights applied, the cursor positioned on the Account ID field, and the keyboard unlocked so the user can make corrections.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display AND the informational message area is empty (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is set to TRUE, indicating no informational message has been populated)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen setup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the prompt message 'Enter or update id of account to display' as the active input prompt (WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT is set to TRUE), and this prompt is rendered in a dark or dimmed color on the screen to indicate it is a guidance message rather than a data value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Prompt Message When No Informational Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the informational message area on the Account View screen is empty (no info message has been set), the system should automatically set and display a prompt message guiding the user to enter or update the account ID they wish to view.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display AND the informational message area contains a message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is FALSE, meaning WS-INFO-MSG has been populated with a value such as 'Displaying details of given Account')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen attribute setup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the informational message from WS-INFO-MSG in the INFOMSGO field on the screen, and the informational message area color attribute (INFOMSGC) is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), indicating that a valid informational message is actively being shown to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Confirmation Message When Account Data Is Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When account data has been successfully retrieved and is being displayed on the Account View screen, the informational message area should show a confirmation message 'Displaying details of given Account' rendered in a neutral color to indicate active data display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured AND the informational message area is empty (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display color attributes for the informational message area on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message area color attribute (INFOMSGC of CACTVWAO) is set to dark or dimmed (DFHBMDAR), visually indicating to the user that no active informational message is present and the area contains only a background prompt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Dark Color to Informational Message Area When No Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the informational message area is empty (no info message set), the system must render the informational message area in a dark or dimmed color on the Account View screen to visually distinguish it from active informational content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured AND the informational message area contains an active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE flag is FALSE, meaning WS-INFO-MSG has been populated)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display color attributes for the informational message area on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message area color attribute (INFOMSGC of CACTVWAO) is set to neutral color (DFHNEUTR), visually indicating to the user that an active informational message is present and should be read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Neutral Color to Informational Message Area When Message Is Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the informational message area contains an active message (such as a confirmation that account details are being displayed), the system must render the informational message area in a neutral color on the Account View screen to indicate active informational content.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid Account ID has passed all input validations AND the system is about to begin the account data retrieval process (entering the 9000-READ-ACCT routine)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account data retrieval process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The informational message flag is reset to indicate no informational message exists (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is set to TRUE), clearing any prior informational message state so that the screen message area reflects the outcome of the current retrieval attempt

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Informational Message State at Start of Account Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of every account data retrieval attempt, the informational message state is reset to 'no info message', ensuring that any previously displayed informational message is cleared before new account data lookup results are evaluated and a fresh message state is established.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen variables are being set up for display AND the informational message working storage field (WS-INFO-MSG) contains a message value (e.g., 'Displaying details of given Account')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen output fields with current data values
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The content of the informational message working storage field (WS-INFO-MSG) is moved to the informational message output field (INFOMSGO of CACTVWAO) on the Account View screen, making the message visible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Informational Message Field on Screen from Message Storage
all_rules.Rule_Description: During screen variable setup, the current informational message stored in the working storage message field is transferred to the screen's informational message output field, ensuring the user sees the most current informational message (such as 'Displaying details of given Account') on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to return control to the CICS transaction manager and there is a pending return message or error message stored in the working storage return message field (WS-RETURN-MSG)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return control sequence is initiated at the COMMON-RETURN point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The content of the working storage return message field (WS-RETURN-MSG) must be copied into the communication area error message field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG) so that the message is preserved and available for display during the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Propagate Return Message to Communication Area Error Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before returning control to the transaction manager, any pending return or error message held in the working storage return message field must be copied into the communication area error message field so it is available for display on the next screen interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is preparing to return control and the main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains current session context including the calling program, destination program, user type, last mapset used, and last map used
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return control sequence is initiated at the COMMON-RETURN point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire content of the main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be copied into the first portion of the outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA), preserving all program navigation context, user type, and map/mapset information for the next program interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Package Main Application Communication Area into Outgoing Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: The main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which holds shared application context including program navigation details, user type, and last map and mapset used, must be packaged into the first portion of the outgoing communication area before returning control.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The main application communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has already been packaged into the first portion of the outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contains the current program-level state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return control sequence is initiated at the COMMON-RETURN point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The content of the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be placed into the outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA) starting at the position immediately after the end of the main application communication area (offset = length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1), for a length equal to the size of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA, ensuring both areas are preserved contiguously in the outgoing communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Append Program-Specific Communication Area into Second Portion of Outgoing Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which holds state information specific to this Account View program, must be appended into the second portion of the outgoing communication area immediately after the main application communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully assembled with both the main application communication area and the program-specific communication area, and the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) identifies this Account View transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return control sequence completes at the COMMON-RETURN point
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control must be returned to the CICS transaction manager specifying: (1) the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) so the same transaction is re-invoked on the next user action, (2) the fully assembled outgoing communication area (WS-COMMAREA) containing all session context, and (3) the full length of the outgoing communication area — ensuring the screen remains active and all session state is available for the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to Transaction Manager Keeping Screen Active for Further User Interaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After packaging all session and program-specific context into the outgoing communication area, control must be returned to the CICS transaction manager specifying the current transaction ID and the fully assembled communication area, so the screen remains active and the session state is preserved for the next user interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the Account ID field color is being initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen attribute setup process begins for the Account ID field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID field color is set to the default color, clearing any previously applied color formatting before conditional rules are evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Account ID Field to Default Color on Screen Load
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before applying any conditional highlighting, the Account ID field on the Account View screen is always reset to the default display color as a baseline, ensuring no residual color from a previous state is carried forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display after the user submitted an Account ID value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID entered by the user is determined to be invalid — specifically, the value is either non-numeric or equals zero (Account Filter Not-OK flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID field on the screen is highlighted in RED color to visually indicate to the user that the entered account number is invalid and must be corrected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Highlight Account ID Field in RED When Invalid Account Number Entered
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters an account number that fails validation because it is non-numeric or equals zero, the Account ID field must be visually highlighted in RED to alert the user that the entered value is invalid and requires correction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the user has previously interacted with this screen (re-entry state is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Account ID field was left blank (empty, spaces, or asterisk submitted) by the user on this return visit (Account Filter Blank flag is set AND program re-entry flag is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An asterisk character (*) is placed in the Account ID field as a visual placeholder, AND the Account ID field is highlighted in RED color to indicate that a required Account ID value was not provided

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Asterisk Placeholder and Highlight Account ID Field in RED When Blank on Re-entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a returning user (re-entering the screen after a prior interaction) submits the screen without providing any Account ID value, the Account ID field must display an asterisk (*) as a visual placeholder and be highlighted in RED, signaling that the required Account ID was not provided.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has submitted an Account ID for lookup and the Card Cross-Reference file does not contain a record matching the submitted Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Cross-Reference file lookup returns a 'Not Found' result for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Filter status must be set to 'Invalid' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK) AND the overall Input status must be set to 'Error' (INPUT-ERROR), indicating that the submitted account cannot be processed further

all_rules.Rule_Name: Flag Account as Invalid When Not Found in Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file returns no matching record, the account filter must be marked as invalid and the overall input must be flagged as an error, regardless of whether a prior error message already exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the account filter has been marked as invalid and input flagged as error
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the error message area is currently empty (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is TRUE, meaning no prior error message has been set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the error message area is empty, proceed to build a new formatted error message; If the error message area already contains a prior message, skip message construction and preserve the existing error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check for Existing Error Message Before Building New Account Not Found Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before constructing a new error message for an account not found in the Cross-Reference file, the system must check whether an error message has already been set. If a prior error message exists, it must be preserved and no new message is constructed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the error message area is currently empty (no prior error message exists)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to build the account not found error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system response code from the file lookup attempt must be captured into ERROR-RESP AND the system reason code from the file lookup attempt must be captured into ERROR-RESP2, making both codes available for inclusion in the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Response and Reason Codes for Account Not Found Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Cross-Reference file and no prior error message exists, the system response code and reason code from the failed file lookup must be captured and stored so they can be included in the error message displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the error message area is currently empty AND the response code and reason code from the failed lookup have been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system constructs the account not found error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A single formatted error message must be built by concatenating all of the following components in order: the literal text 'Account:' + the searched Account ID (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) + the literal text ' not found in Cross ref file.  Resp:' + the captured Response Code (ERROR-RESP) + the literal text ' Reas:' + the captured Reason Code (ERROR-RESP2), and the resulting message must be stored in the error message field (WS-RETURN-MSG) for display on the Account View screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Formatted Error Message for Account Not Found in Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file and no prior error message exists, a detailed formatted error message must be constructed by combining the literal label 'Account:', the actual Account ID that was searched, the phrase 'not found in Cross ref file', the response code prefixed with 'Resp:', and the reason code prefixed with 'Reas:' into a single message string.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A formatted error message has been built combining the account ID, 'not found in Cross ref file' text, response code, and reason code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The STRING operation completes building the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete formatted error message must be stored in WS-RETURN-MSG, which is the field used to display error messages on the Account View screen (ERRMSGO of CACTVWAO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Formatted Account Not Found Error Message for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully constructed account not found error message must be stored in the designated screen error message field so it can be presented to the user on the Account View screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID lookup in the Card Cross-Reference file has returned a 'Not Found' result AND the account filter has been marked as invalid AND the input has been flagged as an error AND the error message has been set (either newly built or pre-existing)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue with the next step in the account data retrieval chain (Account Master lookup)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must immediately stop all further account data lookups — specifically, the Account Master file lookup (9300-GETACCTDATA-BYACCT) and the Customer Master file lookup (9400-GETCUSTDATA-BYCUST) must NOT be executed — and control must return to the Account View processing to display the error to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Further Account Data Lookups When Account Not Found in Cross-Reference
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, all subsequent data lookups (Account Master and Customer Master) must be immediately halted. The account lookup chain is a sequential dependency — without a valid Cross-Reference record, neither account details nor customer details can be retrieved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account lookup has been performed against the Account Master file and the account was not found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the error message display area is currently empty (no prior error message has been set during this transaction)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the error message area is empty, the system proceeds to construct a new formatted error message using the searched account ID; if an error message already exists, the system skips message construction and retains the existing error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check If Error Message Area Is Empty Before Constructing Account Not Found Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Account Master file, the system must first check whether an error message has already been set before constructing a new one, to avoid overwriting a prior error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account lookup against the Account Master file returned a 'not found' result AND the error message area is currently empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to build the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system takes the actual account ID value that was used in the search (WS-CARD-RID-ACCT-ID-X) to be included in the error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Searched Account ID for Error Message Construction
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the error message area is confirmed to be empty and an account was not found in the Account Master file, the system retrieves the actual account ID that was searched so it can be included in the error message for user clarity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account lookup against the Account Master file returned a 'not found' result AND the error message area is currently empty AND the searched account ID is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the error message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system combines the following elements into a single formatted error message string in this exact order: the literal text 'Account:', followed by the actual account ID that was searched, followed by ' not found in', followed by ' Acct Master file.Resp:', followed by the system response code, followed by ' Reas:', followed by the system reason code — and stores the resulting message in the error message display area (WS-RETURN-MSG)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Construct Formatted Account Not Found Error Message for Account Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Account Master file and no prior error message exists, the system constructs a detailed, human-readable error message by combining the literal label, the searched account ID, a descriptive not-found phrase, and the system response and reason codes into a single formatted string.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The formatted error message string has been constructed combining the account ID, not-found description, and system response and reason codes
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The string construction is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The fully formatted error message is stored in the error message display area (WS-RETURN-MSG) which is used to display messages to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Formatted Error Message in Error Message Display Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: After constructing the formatted account-not-found error message, the system stores it in the designated error message display area so it can be presented to the user on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account lookup against the Account Master file has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account ID is not found in the Account Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the overall input as an error (INPUT-ERROR flag set to TRUE) AND marks the account filter/input field as invalid (FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK set to TRUE), which stops further processing of account and customer data retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Account Filter as Invalid When Account Not Found in Account Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Account Master file, the system must mark the account input as invalid and flag an input error, preventing any further data retrieval steps from proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account lookup against the Account Master file returned a 'not found' result
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the error message area and finds that an error message has already been set (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF is FALSE, meaning a message is already present)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system skips the construction of a new error message entirely and retains the existing error message in the error message display area without modification

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Error Message Construction When Prior Error Message Already Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an account is not found in the Account Master file but an error message has already been set earlier in the same transaction, the system preserves the existing error message and does not overwrite it with a new one.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer lookup has been performed using a Customer ID, and the Customer ID was not found in the Customer Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether an existing error message is already set for the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If an error message already exists, the system retains the existing message and does not construct a new error message; if no error message exists, the system proceeds to build a new formatted error message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Prevent Overwriting Existing Error Message When Customer Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer lookup fails because the Customer ID does not exist in the Customer Master File, the system must check whether an error message is already present before constructing a new one. If a message already exists, it is preserved and no new message is built.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer lookup has been performed using a Customer ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer ID is not found in the Customer Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the transaction as having an input error and flags the customer filter as not valid, halting any further data retrieval or display of customer information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Transaction as Invalid When Customer Not Found in Customer Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer lookup fails because the Customer ID does not exist in the Customer Master File, the system must flag the transaction as containing an input error and mark the customer filter as invalid, preventing further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer lookup has failed because the Customer ID does not exist in the Customer Master File, and no prior error message is currently set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the error message to inform the user of the failed lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs a single formatted error message string by combining in sequence: the label 'CustId:', the actual Customer ID value that was searched, the text ' not found in customer master', the system response code labeled 'Resp: ', and the system reason code labeled 'REAS:', and stores this combined message as the current error message for screen display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Construct Formatted Error Message When Customer ID Not Found
