all_rules.Rule_Description: When a customer is not found in the Customer Master File and no prior error message exists, the system constructs a detailed, formatted error message by concatenating the literal label 'CustId:', the actual Customer ID that was searched, the literal text ' not found in customer master', the system response code prefixed by 'Resp: ', and the system reason code prefixed by 'REAS:' into a single message string for display to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is constructing an error message because a Customer ID was not found in the Customer Master File and no prior error message exists
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error message string is being assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The actual Customer ID value that was searched (WS-CARD-RID-CUST-ID-X) is embedded within the error message immediately after the label 'CustId:', making the specific missing customer identifiable to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Include Actual Customer ID in Not-Found Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The error message for a customer not found condition must include the specific Customer ID value that was used in the lookup, so the user can identify exactly which customer record was not found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer lookup has failed because the Customer ID does not exist in the Customer Master File, and no prior error message is currently set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assembles the formatted error message string
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system appends the system response code (labeled 'Resp: ') and the system reason code (labeled 'REAS:') to the end of the error message string, ensuring the complete diagnostic information is included in the single formatted message presented to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve System Response and Reason Codes in Customer Not-Found Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When constructing the customer not-found error message, the system must capture and include both the system response code and the system reason code in the formatted message to provide complete diagnostic context about why the customer record could not be retrieved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the informational message area (WS-INFO-MSG) contains no active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen setup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the informational message to the standard prompt text 'Enter or update id of account to display' (WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT is set to TRUE), guiding the user to provide an Account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Prompt Text When No Informational Message Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the informational message area is empty (no active message has been set), the system automatically sets the informational message to prompt the user to enter or update the Account ID they wish to view.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen is being prepared for display and the informational message area (WS-INFO-MSG) already contains an active message such as 'Displaying details of given Account'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the state of the informational message area during screen setup and finds that WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is false
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retains the existing informational message as-is and moves it to the screen output field (INFOMSGO), so the user sees the current status message without any overwrite

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retain Existing Informational Message When Already Set
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an informational message is already present (e.g., 'Displaying details of given Account' after a successful account lookup), the system retains and displays that existing message without overwriting it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured and the informational message area contains no active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display color attribute for the informational message field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system applies a dark/dimmed color attribute (DFHBMDAR) to the informational message display area (INFOMSGC), visually suppressing the field since no message is active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Informational Message Display Color to Dark When No Active Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When there is no active informational message to display, the informational message area on screen is rendered in a dark or dimmed color, visually indicating to the user that no status information is currently available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account View screen attributes are being configured and the informational message area contains an active message (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE condition is false)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the display color attribute for the informational message field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system applies a neutral color attribute (DFHNEUTR) to the informational message display area (INFOMSGC), ensuring the active message is clearly visible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Informational Message Display Color to Neutral When Active Message Present
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an active informational message exists and is ready to be shown to the user, the informational message area is rendered in a neutral (standard) color, making the message clearly visible and readable on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The informational message content (WS-INFO-MSG mapped to INFOMSGO) and its display color attribute (INFOMSGC) have both been set, and the full screen output area (CACTVWAO) is ready
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the Account View screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is displayed with the informational message area showing either the prompt text 'Enter or update id of account to display' in dark/dimmed color (when no active message) or the status message 'Displaying details of given Account' in neutral color (when an active message is present), with the cursor positioned and the keyboard unlocked for user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Informational Message Content on Account View Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the informational message content and display color have been determined, the system renders the complete Account View screen including the informational message area, making the prompt or status message visible to the user.

description:
COACTVWC is an online CICS program that accepts and processes Account View requests, allowing users to look up and display detailed account and associated customer information by entering an account number. The program validates the input account number, retrieves account data from the Card Cross-Reference file, Account Master file, and Customer Master file, then presents the consolidated account and customer details on screen. It is a main/driver program that handles navigation via PF keys, including returning to the calling program or main menu.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS Files - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Entry and Context Initialization - Determine if this is a fresh entry or re-entry by checking communication area length and originating program. Initialize working storage and communication area accordingly to establish the correct processing context. 2: PF Key Validation - Validate the function key pressed by the user. Accept only Enter key or PF3 as valid inputs. If any other key is pressed, treat it as an Enter key press to continue normal processing. 3: Navigation to Previous Screen or Main Menu (PF3 Handler) - When user presses PF3, determine the calling program and transaction. If no calling program is identified, navigate to the main menu; otherwise, return control to the originating program, passing updated communication area. 4: Display Initial Account View Screen - When the program is entered for the first time (fresh entry), display a blank Account View screen prompting the user to enter an account number to display. 5: Screen Header Initialization - Populate the screen header with application title, transaction ID, program name, current system date (MM/DD/YY format), and current system time (HH:MM:SS format). 6: Account Data Population on Screen - If account data was successfully retrieved, populate the screen with account details including: active status, current balance, credit limit, cash credit limit, current cycle credit, current cycle debit, open date, expiration date, reissue date, and group ID. 7: Customer Data Population on Screen - If customer data was successfully retrieved, populate the screen with customer details including: customer ID, SSN (formatted as XXX-XX-XXXX), FICO credit score, date of birth, first/middle/last name, address lines, city, state, zip code, country, phone numbers 1 and 2, government-issued ID, EFT account ID, and primary card holder indicator. 8: Screen Field Attribute and Color Setup - Set screen field attributes including cursor positioning on the account ID field. Apply red color highlighting to the account ID field when it contains an error or is blank during re-entry. Set informational message display color based on whether a message exists. 9: Receive User Input from Screen - Capture the data entered by the user on the Account View screen, specifically the account number input field. 10: Account Number Input Validation - Validate the account number entered by the user: (a) Check if account number is blank or not provided - set error message prompting for account number; (b) Check if account number is non-numeric or equals zero - set error message requiring an 11-digit non-zero numeric account number; (c) If valid, store the account number for further processing. 11: Cross-Field Validation - After individual field validation, check if no search criteria were provided at all (account filter is blank) and set appropriate 'No input received' message. 12: Account Card Cross-Reference Lookup - Look up the provided account ID in the Card Cross-Reference file using the account ID as the key. If found, retrieve and store the associated customer ID and card number. If not found, set an error message indicating the account was not found in the cross-reference file. 13: Account Master Data Retrieval - Read the Account Master file using the account ID to retrieve full account details. If found, mark account as found for screen display. If not found, set an error message indicating the account was not found in the account master file. 14: Customer Master Data Retrieval - Using the customer ID obtained from the card cross-reference, read the Customer Master file to retrieve full customer details. If found, mark customer as found for screen display. If not found, set an error message indicating the customer was not found in the customer master file. 15: Account View Processing Orchestration - Coordinate the complete account retrieval sequence: first look up the card cross-reference by account ID, then retrieve account master data, then retrieve customer master data. Stop processing and display error if any step fails. 16: Error Message Display and Screen Refresh - When input validation errors occur, display the Account View screen again with appropriate error messages highlighted in red, with the cursor positioned on the account ID field for correction. 17: Informational Message Management - Manage the informational message area on the screen: display 'Enter or update id of account to display' as a prompt when no info message exists, or display 'Displaying details of given Account' when account data is being shown. 18: Return Control with Communication Area - Package the communication area (including program context, last map/mapset used) and return control to the CICS transaction manager, specifying the current transaction ID so the screen remains active for further user interaction.
